Julius Randle has brutal response to Nets' blowout loss: 'One of the worst games I've ever been a part of'

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Brooklyn Nets are no strangers to losing games this season, as they fell to 3-11 on Wednesday night, but in a season filled with lopsided defeats, losing by 30 points to the Chicago Bulls stood out as a fresh low point.

In a recent development, the Bulls also entered Wednesday's game at 3-10 on the season, operating as one of the league's worst teams so far, but Chicago exploded for 137 points against the Nets, with eight players reaching double figures. While Chicago's biggest issue has come on the defensive end this season, the Bulls haven't exactly been lighting opponents up offensively, sitting 23rd in the league in offensive rating.

The Nets' complete inability to put up a resistance against the Bulls rang alarm bells in Brooklyn and had veteran Julius Randle calling out his team for an "embarrassing" and "unacceptable" performance.

According to recent reports, "I've been in the league for 13 years... that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of."Julius Randle didn't hold back after the Nets’ 30-point loss to Bulls. 😳 pic.twitter.com/s3YQ8TxP35.

Recent findings suggest that "The main struggle? I don't know, that was embarrassing," Randle said after the game. "Been in the league for 13 years and that's one of the worst games I've ever been a part of. And not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes -- it's just a bad night -- but it's how we did it. That just, it wasn't cool. Nothing about it was cool. We gotta find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just is unacceptable.".

Considering Randle has been on his fair share of bad basketball teams over his career in Los Angeles, Newly introduced Orleans and New York, that's saying something.

There are five teams that have separated themselves from the pack at the bottom of the NBA in terms of defense and the Nets are one of them with a 119.0 defensive rating (26th in the league). No one expected much of Brooklyn on that end of the floor with the roster they've assembled, but it's one thing to have lesser talent on the defensive end; it's another to combine that with a general lack of effort.

This early in the season, the latter is a much larger concern and the Nets have now given up at least 124 points in five of their last six games. If they were able to shrug off some of those lopsided losses to quality teams as life in the NBA, Wednesday was proof that their problems extend far beyond just some schedule losses.

Giving up 137 to a Bulls team that's been similarly bad this year is, in Randle's words, unacceptable. The concern is that no one in Brooklyn, including Randle, seems quite sure what the exact problem is or how to fix it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're in the throes of spooky season, and fittingly, the New Jersey Devils just got a lot scarier with the acquisition of superstar goaltender Connor Hellebuyck.

Industry observers note that one of the best goaltenders in the world, Hellebuyck fills the biggest need on the Devils roster. With him in between the pipes and an electrifying group of forwards, Newly introduced Jersey will be a force in the Eastern Conference.

Don't take my word for it. Just look at what the Devils did Tuesday against the Dallas Stars. In his first start with the team, Hellebuyck stopped 17 of the 18 shots he faced -- allowing one goal on 2.04 expected goals against -- in a 5-1 victory.

Nico Hischier, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes each had multi-point nights as the Devils took full advantage of the chances they created against a stout Dallas team. This type of game has to be exactly what general manager Sunny Mehta envisioned when he swung the deal for Hellebuyck.

Moving forward, the Devils will be burdened with the pressure that comes along with being a bona fide Cup contender. For a franchise that's fallen short of expectations a few times lately, that can be a scary prospect, and it inspired a special Halloween edition of the NHL Power Rankings in which I highlight the scariest thing about each team.

    #119191. Logan Webb landing spots: Five possible destinations for Giants starting pitcher on the trading block

    Logan Webb landing spots: Five possible destinations for Giants starting pitcher on the trading block

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (697 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason.
    • Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal.
    • Which teams might make for a good fit for Webb?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason. Sure enough, they are "listening to trade offers" for All-Star starting pitcher Logan Webb, per The Athletic, but they'd need a "very strong return" in order to deal him.

    Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal. He went 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.3 WAR last season, but it was his worst year in quite a while. He averaged 4.5 WAR per season in the previous four years with a 3.22 ERA and led the National League in innings pitched from 2023 to 2025, racking up three straight top-six Cy Young finishes.

    Which teams might make for a good fit for Webb? Many of them. We're talking about a workhorse under team control for two more years. Let's run through five of the best fits while, again, knowing that basically any contender should be interested in at least a conversation with the Giants.

    Recent findings suggest that the Cubs need so much pitching this offseason. Their entire rotation heading into the playoffs last season is in free agency. This isn't hyperbole. Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson are all off the roster. If the Cubs were to try and put together a rotation right now, it would be something like Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and several question marks. Ben Brown and Cade Horton will open the season on the injured list.

    Do we really need to spell out what a reliable innings eater would mean for this bunch? Webb is an outstanding fit here.

    It has been revealed that the upstart playoff team last season was a ton of fun, but also was running bullpen games in the ALDS. The White Sox just attached Davis Martin to Luis Castillo in a trade to the Rockies in order to offload Castillo's contract, too, so they're down a starter. The Dustin May signing means they have him along with Sean Burke and converted reliever Grant Taylor. The White Sox would reportedly like to sign another starter in the May ballpark, but what about trading for someone better like Webb?

    A top four in the rotation of Webb, Burke, Taylor and May would be exponentially better than what the Sox had last season.

    Sources indicate that returns of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach at some point will help, but this is still a thin rotation for a team coming off a division title. Chris Sale remains, but he's followed up with Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder before the Spencers return. Youngster Didier Fuentes moving to the rotation is exciting, but there are an awful lot of questions behind Sale, who turns 38 in late March, by the way.

    Industry observers note that given that the Padres reside in the NL West with the Giants, there might be a bit of an intradivision tax in terms of the asking price, but Padres boss A.J. Preller is never shy about offloading prospects. There could certainly be a fit. The Padres need rotation help, too, after losing Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and others to free agency. We know they're in on Tarik Skubal, but that doesn't mean they'll be content with just landing one substantial fish.

    Look at the current Padres rotation. It's basically Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez. With three straight playoff berths and zero trips to the World Series, now isn't the time to have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig make up 60% of the rotation.

    Dealing for Webb and signing Skubal would make for a nice offseason for fresh ownership, no?

    One of the most disappointing teams in baseball last season needs to have a prolific offseason. We've heard plenty about the Mets being involved in the Skubal sweepstakes and we've seen them win a monster bidding war before (see: Soto, Juan). Grabbing Webb would make it quite a well-rounded rotation with talented youngsters Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case.

    We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there.

    Recent findings suggest that tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and noted that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers").

    The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

    The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

    In a recent development, the Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

    Gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

    The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

    The Red Sox also reportedly showed interest.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight new signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

    Not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

    Recent findings suggest that this meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

    According to recent reports, it proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

    It has been revealed that roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined plan, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” said Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

    "He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

    According to recent reports, for Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

    Recent findings suggest that de Zerbi remarked he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

    "I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

    Industry observers note that newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

    Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm.

    Sources indicate that what a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY.

    Industry observers note that “After the first goal we lost confidence,” mentioned De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

    In a recent development, to be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the latest signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

    Of the five upcoming arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

    "He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA.

    Industry observers note that might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

    There are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

    At least the problems facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

    The Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too major. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

    “At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

    “We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

    In a recent development, speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach remarked: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match proposal at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

    Recent findings suggest that “We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

    Both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

    Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

    Subs: Dubravka, Senesi, Gallagher, Udogie, Bergvall, Solanke, Kudus, Davies, Moore.

    Newcastle: Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Miley, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Wissa.

    Subs: Jaouen, Schar, Bamba, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Woltemade, Ramsey, Shahar.

    In a recent development, recent recruit Nico Gonzalez begins in midfield and is set to make his Newcastle debut. Joe Willock scored in the Liverpool draw and is rewarded with a start, replacing the injured Will Osula.

    Nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB.

    Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

    Industry observers note that marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

    Good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of new Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

    Recent findings suggest that as expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his upcoming club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

    In a recent development, our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi.

    Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

    Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

    In a recent development, nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

    Newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his fresh surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

    It has been revealed that despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in newly introduced boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

    Newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

    A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

    Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the Latest York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post.
    • Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.
    • Industry observers note that skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the Latest York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.

    Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.

    Industry observers note that skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up:.

    According to recent reports, "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He showed few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Industry observers note that over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality.

    Since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal.

    In a recent development, the nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.

    In a recent development, coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, big-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette.

    Sources indicate that further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031.

    The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like:.

    Given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal. That last spot in the rotation, as such, should be ticketed to someone else outside the organization at present, whether a free agent or a trade acquisition.

    The landing of the top free agent available no doubt ramps up the pressure on Stearns and the Mets to deliver a playoff berth and a deep October run in 2027, but Skubal's presence also makes it much likely that such a feat comes to pass.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • According to recent reports, kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    According to recent reports, kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Industry observers note that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    It's important to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    Industry observers note that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Industry observers note that montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    Recent findings suggest that we already know the Wild are massive-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    According to recent reports, however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    With Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    Sources indicate that it was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't at the moment have on their roster.

    Sources indicate that carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    According to recent reports, utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    In a recent development, dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    #119179. Industry News: NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1751 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: NBA's eight biggest disappointments through one month: Injury bug, same old East and an underwhelming champ

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1751 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects.
    • In other areas, things are going … not so well.
    • It has been revealed that there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're roughly one month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and things are going pretty well in certain respects. Luka Dončić and the Lakers are off to a hot start in Los Angeles. Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs have picked up right where they left off after last season's Finals trip. And the Celtics are battling the latest-look Sixers at the top of the Eastern Conference.

    In other areas, things are going … not so well. Below are the eight biggest disappointments so far this season.

    It has been revealed that there have been so many players impacted by various injuries that it's almost hard to keep track. Jalen Duren (hamstring) has missed almost the entire season in Detroit. Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are still recovering from knee injuries and have yet to play for Golden State, while Steph Curry is now out with an abdominal tear and Kristaps Porziņģis stepped away from basketball. After sitting out all of last season with an Achilles tear, Tyrese Haliburton is currently dealing with a hamstring matter. Brandon Ingram (Achilles) hasn't made his debut for the Clippers. Austin Reaves is out with a heel injury. Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery and will miss a chunk of time for the Wolves, and it seems unlikely that Donte DiVincenzo (Achilles) will play this season, even though he remains hopeful that he will. Paolo Banchero remains sidelined with an ankle sprain. Ja Morant is out with a hamstring strain. Ben Simmons didn't play a single game for the Kings before tearing his Achilles. Kawhi Leonard (knee) is once again on the shelf in Toronto. And the reeling Jazz are without Jaren Jackson Jr (knee), Lauri Markkanen (hand) and Jusuf Nurkic (toe).

    Recent findings suggest that it's all a huge bummer for the players, their teams and fans of hoops in general. But no team has been hurt more on the injury front than the Thunder.

    Industry observers note that the disappointment here is how unkind fate has been to OKC. The Thunder were close to fully healthy when the season started — and then far from it not long after it began. When OKC beat the Spurs in San Antonio in the season opener — after losing four of five regular season games to them last season, as well as falling to the Spurs in the Western Conference Finals — it felt like a statement that the Thunder were back and we were in for an epic battle between the two teams over who would rule the West.

    In a recent development, and then all of that was stripped away. Just three games into the season, Jalen Williams — who missed much of last season due to injury — suffered a gruesome fall and had to undergo surgery for a fractured fibula as well as reconstruction of ankle ligaments. In that same fateful game, Cason Wallace tore his labrum and later had shoulder surgery. They haven't been officially ruled out, but if either of them plays basketball again this season, it will be a surprise. Making matters worse, Chet Holmgren tore a tendon in his knee and "underwent a biological treatment" to address it. He'll miss approximately two months, but the Thunder do expect him to return. That's what passes for good news in OKC these days.

    The Thunder are — or were — the deepest team in the NBA. That's a credit to what Sam Presti built. But even OKC has its limits. Losing three of five starters is tough to overcome, even when you're led by the reigning back-to-back MVP in Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. That doesn't mean the Thunder (presently 9-6 and eighth in the West) can't still make a deep playoff run, but the odds of them doing so — and of them fighting the Spurs all season for the top spot — got a lot longer.

    We were told that this was finally the season that the East returned to its former glory. We were told that the conference would be loaded. We were wrong. (Full disclosure while putting a palm to my face: I might have done some of that telling.).

    Recent findings suggest that through the first month, the East has been mostly underwhelming. Eight of the 15 teams are below .500. The conference has a combined 17-37 record against the West. Only one of the top seven teams in net rating — the Celtics — plays in the East. Five of the top six teams by point differential play in the West.

    In a recent development, the defending champion Knicks are 8-6. The Cavaliers, who made it to last season's Eastern Conference Finals and had championship aspirations of their own, are 8-8. The Magic, Raptors and Pacers — who at the moment occupy the eight, nine and 10 seeds — all have losing records. By contrast, the worst play-in team in the West right now is Golden State at 8-7. That record would be good enough for the seven seed if they played in the East.

    Sources indicate that but maybe we shouldn't be surprised. Since the 1999-2000 season, the West has had the better overall record in all but three campaigns. Maybe next year the East will finally snap out of its funk, but don't bet on it.

    The Jazz just picked up back-to-back road wins in L.A. over the Lakers and Clippers, but that doesn't begin to dig them out of the deep hole they've made for themselves. The Jazz were gearing up to be competitive in the West this season. So much for that. Like the Thunder, injuries have not been kind to them. Nurkic has yet to play a single game this season, while Markkanen and JJJ have missed significant time with maladies of their own. What looked like a formidable frontcourt has been decimated.

    Sources indicate that still, it's hard to believe how bad the Jazz have been in pretty much every facet. Their first win came in the second game of the season, a one-point squeaker over the Pelicans. It took until mid-November to end an ugly 12-game losing streak and pick up their second and third wins. They're 25th in net rating and point differential. The season has barely begun, and it's already basically wait until next year for the Jazz.

    The NBA panicked and tried to solve for a problem that wasn't actually an matter, except for a small fragment of people who care more about optics than the product itself. And so the league enacted lottery reform and the fresh 3-2-1 system was put in place. This was ostensibly designed to prevent tanking, incentivize winning and bring greater parity to the league. Oops.

    Industry observers note that the Hornets, Wizards, Bulls, Nets and Bucks are all well underwater in the East. The Pelicans and Clippers are drowning in the West, while the Kings and Jazz are even worse. What the league failed to account for is that some of these teams are just organically bad — and now they will have decreased odds at getting better.

    Sources indicate that under the old system, the Grizzlies would be pretty thrilled to see the Jazz struggling since Memphis has Utah's first-round pick in the upcoming draft as part of the JJJ trade. Alas, after making that move, the league changed the rules, which means the Grizzlies can pick no higher than sixth now as a consequence of the new system preventing a team from picking in the top five in three consecutive drafts.     In a recent development, and on top of it all, fans of bad teams were robbed of the entertaining-in-its-own-way race to the bottom to maximize lottery odds, giving supporters a small silver lining in the otherwise gray clouds of their season. RIP Tank Watch.

    Sources indicate that when aren't the Kings disappointing? Aside from their unsightly 1-13 record, the Sacramento front office continues to make baffling decisions. The Kings originally acquired Nique Clifford from the Thunder for a Spurs 2027 first-round pick. Sacramento held onto Clifford for 83 games — choosing to bury him on the bench this season and play him barely six minutes per game — before shipping him back to the Thunder for two second-round picks.

    So the Thunder ended up with the player and a first and the Kings ended up with two seconds.

    In a recent development, one of these organizations is savvy and opportunistic, and the other is the Kings. It's a miracle they nailed the Darius Acuff pick.

    Oof. It has not been a good season to date for Bridges. After going cold to begin their first-round playoff series against the Hawks, Bridges found his form and played well, helping the Knicks go on an epic run that ended with New York's first championship in 53 years.

    If that hope was that Bridges would snap out of his early-season funk in similar fashion, the Knicks seem somewhat less patient these days. While head coach Mike Brown has insisted that Bridges is a starter, he has sometimes hedged his bets in crucial situations, going with Landry Shamet or Deuce McBride over Bridges when things get tight and the Knicks need more reliable offense on the floor.

    Through 14 games, Bridges is averaging 7.5 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.1 assists on 40.2/28.9/75 shooting splits. It's the lowest scoring output and the worst shooting numbers of his career. As a result, his minutes have dipped to 25.6 per contest. That's also a career low. Bridges is still a plus defender. And he's only 30. The Knicks obviously hope he'll figure it out, as he has in the past. If not, his new four-year, $150 million extension that kicked in this season will start to look worrisome.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.
    • The first 15 games of the season have been enough for some teams to learn the harsh truth about not being a contender this year, while others are off to surprisingly good starts that could turn them into midseason buyers.
    • It has been revealed that the one unknown this season is how the league's lottery reform will affect the in-season trade market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The 2026-27 NBA season is barely a month old and trade season won't officially begin until December 15 when players signed this summer are eligible to be moved, but that doesn't stop the rumor machine from churning in the Association.

    The first 15 games of the season have been enough for some teams to learn the harsh truth about not being a contender this year, while others are off to surprisingly good starts that could turn them into midseason buyers. That's how the trade market starts to take shape, and with a trade request already made in Upcoming Orleans by Dejounte Murray and a handful of expiring contracts known to be open to moving, we can start piecing together an early look at what trade season may look like.

    It has been revealed that the one unknown this season is how the league's lottery reform will affect the in-season trade market. Fewer teams will have incentive to completely bottom out, but even with teams not trying to sell everything off, there will still be enough teams trying to buy to create a market.

    On Thursday, we got a fresh batch of rumors, starting with some updates on potential suitors for Murray after being sent home by the Pelicans.

    Recent findings suggest that murray makes $32.8 million this year and has a player option for $30.8 million next year that he will almost assuredly pick up. That means he's not exactly a coveted asset, and even for teams with a potential need at point guard, so far no one seems to be jumping at the opportunity to trade for the disgruntled Pelicans guard.

    Two teams that were rapidly connected as potential destinations for Murray were the Suns and the Heat, both with glaring point guard needs and a desire to contend this season. However, neither team is desperate to make a move right now, according to Jake Fischer in the latest Stein Line newsletter.

    Murray and Klutch Sports see Phoenix as a good landing spot, but the Suns view center as a bigger need than point guard and would demand that the Pelicans send back draft capital to take on Murray's salary, Fischer reports. Miami, meanwhile, has shown little appetite for Murray and he is not expected to be one of its trade targets because of his player option for next season that would severely limit their ability to retool the roster around Giannis Antetokounmpo.

    With the two most obvious potential suitors for Murray not exactly showing a lot of excitement for bringing him in, it seems likely that Murray's trade request and absence from the Pelicans will extend for quite some time and could last all the way to the trade deadline.

    Industry observers note that the Washington Wizards are 5-11 to start the season, which makes it increasingly unlikely they will be trying to work out a long-term extension for Davis. The early returns on Washington's commitment to Trae Young have not been good, and if the Wizards are looking to acquire some assets this season, Davis makes the most sense as an expiring contract.

    On the latest episode of the Hoop Collective, ESPN's Brian Windhorst offered an update on Davis' market and desires for his next contract.

    Sources indicate that "I think people have demand for Anthony Davis," Windhorst said. "They just don't want to give him a max extension, and I don't think he's looking for a max extension, but I do think he's looking for a lot of money.".

    That's not exactly groundbreaking information and any team exploring a trade for Davis will want to know what, exactly, he's looking for in his next contract. Below the max is a start, but teams are growing wary of giving out massive money to aging stars in the second apron era. Davis brings an additional level of risk to any long-term contract discussions with his injury history.

    Sources indicate that that said, he has been quite good this season -- averaging 24.6 points and 10.1 rebounds per game on solid efficiency -- and the Wizards should be shopping him to teams desperate for a center upgrade. If Phoenix is less interested in a point guard but has an appetite for a star center, perhaps the Suns could be a trade partner to offload Jalen Green's contract -- to be clear, that's not a rumor, just connecting dots between a few recent rumors.

    Everything with Davis' market will come down to what Davis and Rich Paul tell teams about what they want his next contract to look like.

    With Murray on the block and the Pelicans at 5-11, it's fair to wonder (again) if some of New Orleans' more intriguing players could find their way onto the trade market.

    It has been revealed that the player most teams around the league covet in New Orleans is Trey Murphy III. Even though he's in the midst of a slow start to the season and at the moment dealing with knee tendonitis, other teams still covet his potential as a star on the wing given his abilities as a scorer and defender. The Pelicans also believe strongly in Murphy's upside, and unfortunately for other teams, Fischer reports Murphy -- unlike Murray -- has no desire to make a trade request.

    As such, he's going to be quite expensive to pry from the Pelicans, who "remain reluctant" to discuss trades for Murphy. Given he's their best potential trade chip, that's probably a wise approach, and Newly introduced Orleans will hope some hopeful contender is desperate enough to give up a haul of assets before they consider moving him.

    #119175. Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1267 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Why a long-term mega deal for Tarik Skubal isn't actually all that risky

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1267 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.
    • The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.
    • Industry observers note that let's stop right there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The big prize of this free agent class, ace lefty and two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, has landed with the Mets on a nine-year, $450 million deal.

    The knee-jerk reaction to a contract of this size in many corners will be that he won't possibly be "worth" that much and that such a deal would be a huge "risk" to the signing team.

    Industry observers note that let's stop right there. I don't think it's all that risky. There's risk for the team on every contract, especially pitchers, of course, but in Skubal, the Mets are getting a surefire ace for nearly a decade.

    Let's examine some of the reasons why such an enormous deal isn't actually that dangerous.

    Industry observers note that since returning from surgery in 2023, Skubal has been absurdly good. Across his ages 26-29 seasons, he's made 103 starts and has gone 50-20 with a 2.47 ERA (169 ERA+), 0.92 WHIP and 757 strikeouts in 626 ⅓ innings. He's only walked 109, or 1.6 per nine innings. He rarely gets hit hard, he rarely gives up many runs, he strikes out a high number of hitters and rarely walks any. Simply, he's been good at everything.

    The recent track record here claims this is the best pitcher in baseball, at least in the long view (we could argue Paul Skenes was better in 2025 and Jacob Misiorowski was better in 2026, to name two examples, but if we looked at 2023-present, it isn't all that close).

    There isn't a dropoff in the postseason, either. In eight playoff starts, Skubal has a 2.13 ERA, 0.79 WHIP and 70 strikeouts against nine unintentional walks in 50 ⅔ innings.

    Sources indicate that he's stellar. Pretty much all the time.

    Also, the career workload isn't anything to be concerned about. Skubal heads to his age-30 season now with only 925 ⅓ innings in the regular season. Even counting the playoffs doesn't get Skubal to 1,000 innings at the massive-league level. Let's go back to Skenes. He's only 24 years old and already has 495 career innings. Another ace? Justin Verlander had 1,553 ⅔ career innings through his age-29 season.

    There just isn't a ton of tread on these Skubal tires.

    We'll hear plenty of consternation about Skubal being 30 years old next season as it relates to signing a long-term deal. We'll also hear people say a deal is risky due to his injury history. He had Tommy John surgery in college, flexor tendon surgery in 2022 and arthroscopic surgery (a new procedure using a Nanoscope) in 2026.

    The simple matter is that pretty much every pitcher nowadays has had some sort of surgery on his arm, notably the elbow, and we've seen pitchers time and again bounce back after elbow surgery to perform at a high level.

    In a recent development, skubal just did it. He only missed roughly six weeks after his procedure this past season. He came back to make 19 starts after the surgery and posted a 2.73 ERA with 141 strikeouts in 115 ⅓ innings.

    Sources indicate that I mentioned Verlander above. Skubal is a multi-time Cy Young winner, so it's acceptable to look at some of the best pitchers in baseball and how they aged into their late-30s in recent memory.

    Again, Skubal will be in his age-30 season in 2027. His nine-year deal means it'll run through his age-38 season.

    For those so worried about the long-term finances of the Cohen family, are you sure you're really worried that Skubal won't be productive through five, six or even all nine years of that deal? Given his track record, talent, pitching arsenal, relatively low workload given his age and how well some of the best pitchers have fared through their mid-30s, he actually seems like a great bet.

    In a recent development, A decade ago, the common talking point was that long and huge deals for pitchers never age well. That isn't actually the case, for the most part. Here are some of the biggest pitcher contracts of all time and how they unfolded (or are unfolding).

    In a recent development, yoshinobu Yamamoto, Dodgers, 12 years, $325 million -- He came over from Japan for his age-25 season, so this one was a different animal. Still, it sure doesn't seem like it'll be a bad deal, does it?

    It has been revealed that gerrit Cole, Yankees, 9 years, $324 million -- Through six years of the deal, Cole has missed a chunk of time due to Tommy John surgery. He's also won a Cy Young, finished top four in Cy Young voting three times, been worth 22.4 WAR and was the ace of an American League pennant winner.

    Stephen Strasburg, Nationals, 7 years, $245 million -- Here's the bust. Strasburg was never healthy again after the 2019 World Series title run. Still, the Nationals wouldn't have that title without him.

    Industry observers note that justin Verlander, Tigers, 10 years, $219.5 million -- This was the deal that ran from 2010-19. During this deal, Verlander won two Cy Youngs (one in the second year of the deal, one in the final year), a World Series, three pennants, 160 games and led the league in pitcher WAR three times.

    Max Fried, Yankees, 8 years, $218 million -- It's only been two years, but Fried is 24-10 with a 2.83 ERA and finished fourth in AL Cy Young voting in his first year.

    In a recent development, david Price, Red Sox, 7 years, $217 million -- He won a World Series in the third year of the contract. Overall, he was 53-26 with a 3.78 ERA (118 ERA+) through the course of the deal.

    Sources indicate that corbin Burnes, Diamondbacks, 6 years, $210 million -- Burnes had his first year of the deal interrupted by Tommy John surgery. He had a 2.66 ERA through 11 starts prior to the injury. The jury's still out, but he heads to his age-32 season fully recovered now.

    Zack Greinke, 6 years, $206.5 million -- Over the course of this deal, Greinke was 77-39 with a 3.55 ERA (125 ERA+) and 19.9 WAR. He had a fourth-place Cy Young finish in there.

    CC Sabathia, 9 years, $202 million -- The Yankees won the World Series in Sabathia's first year there and he started the deal with three straight top-four Cy Young finishes. Overall, during this deal, he was 120-73 with 27.1 WAR and had five straight 200-plus inning seasons.

    In a recent development, max Scherzer, 7 years, $191.4 million -- During this contract, Scherzer won two Cy Youngs, a World Series title and 99 games with a 2.75 ERA. He posted 41.8 WAR. In the seven years on this deal, Scherzer finished in the top five in Cy Young voting six times, with 2020 being the outlier.

    Industry observers note that we can close with this. Some people might not care for such a measure, particularly the salary cap crowd who will be worried about the owners paying too much. Regardless, let's stick with the general belief that each individual WAR (1.0 WAR) is worth a bit over $8 million per season.

    By this measure, Skubal was worth $48.4 million in 2024, $53.7 million in 2025 and $41.7 million last season. Putting aside how much less money he actually made than what he was doing on the field, and knowing everything laid out above, I'll ask a simple question:.

    Are you sure a 9-year, $450 million deal for this guy is a "risk?".

    I think we could argue that it'll be a bargain.

    #119171. Industry News: Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

    📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (764 w)
    📖 Baca
    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Winners and losers of the Tarik Skubal signing: Blue Jays, Dodgers strike out; David Stearns looks nervous

    📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (764 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening.
    • In a recent development, the $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team.
    • Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The best player in a thin free agent class came off the board Sunday evening. Two-time Cy Young winning left-hander Tarik Skubal has agreed to a record nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets. There's a $45 million signing bonus and $30 million in deferred payments. The team has not yet announced the signing but that should happen soon.

    In a recent development, the $450 million contract shatters the previous record for a pitcher, which is Yoshinobu Yamamoto's $325 million contract with the Dodgers, Skubal's most recent team. The $50 million average annual salary also shatters the previous record for a pitcher. That was $43.3 million for Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander during their time with the Mets.

    Here now are our winners and losers from Skubal's monster contract with the Mets.

    Let's start with the obvious: Skubal's a winner because he signed a massive, record-shattering contract. Sign a record deal and you're always a winner in my book. The Mets are a winner because they landed not just the best free agent on the market, but one of the game's best pitchers. Skubal is a power player who can swing a postseason race or a postseason series all by himself. There are very few players like that in the game and now the Mets have one to lead their rotation.

    Boras, Skubal's agent, tends to shatter records, not beat them by just a little bit. Alex Rodriguez's contract with the Rangers is his Mona Lisa: A-Rod's $252 million contract was exactly double the largest contract in the four major North American sports leagues at the time (Kevin Garnett's $126 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves). Boras did it again with Skubal. He obliterated Yamamoto's total guarantee record, Scherzer's and Verlander's shared average annual value record, and also Max Fried's record deal for a lefty ($218 million). Once again, Boras won big.

    According to recent reports, we can add the Padres here too since they were one of the four teams to meet with Skubal in person this past week, though it was always hard to see San Diego beating out the Blue Jays, Dodgers, and Mets. The Dodgers reportedly held the line at a short-term, high-dollar contract similar to Kyle Tucker's deal, which put them at a disadvantage. Still, they no longer have Skubal in their rotation, and he's irreplaceable. The Blue Jays have been trying to sign top free agents for years (Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Juan Soto, etc.) and have yet to land the plane. Point is, these teams met and pursued Skubal, then he signed elsewhere. Ergo, losers.

    With Skubal off the board, the market for second- and third-tier free agent starters should quickly pick up. That group includes Michael King, Freddy Peralta, and Trevor Rogers. Skubal signing this early is a substantial win for everyone, really, and especially the other free agent starters. They have more than a week to negotiate and sign before the owners are expected to lock out the players after the current CBA expires at 11:59 p.m. on Dec. 1. Pitchers are coming off the board fast and furious right now. Expect that to continue for another week or so.

    According to recent reports, to be sure, the Mets' president of baseball operations is a winner because his team now employs Skubal. This is 100% a Steve Cohen contract, though. Stearns has been against long-term contracts for pitchers throughout his career as an executive, even if he mentioned during the GM Meetings that he works on a "case-by-case basis," and it's hard to believe he'd give a pitcher with three elbow surgeries on his resume this contract. It seems likely Cohen was the one pushing this deal across the finish line, and hey, he's the owner; he can do whatever he wants. Stearns is very much against long-term deals for pitchers, though. I imagine he feels at least a wee bit nervous. Plus, he really can't afford another disaster season like 2026.

    In a recent development, once again, the top free agent went with a massive market team. The Mets are signing Skubal this offseason. The Dodgers signed Tucker last offseason. The Mets signed Soto the offseason before that. The Dodgers signed Ohtani the offseason before that. The folks who insist baseball needs a salary cap, both the owners themselves and the fans who lean that way, now have more ammunition for their fight. Settle in. It is very, very likely we're in for months of salary cap debate during an extended lockout. That was true even before Skubal signed.

    #119169. Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1440 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1440 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that NBA teams are remarkably diligent.
    • On Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
    • So, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

    On Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

    So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a latest roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

    According to recent reports, irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

    If they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

    In a recent development, the question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they initiative to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

    Recent findings suggest that adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

    Recent findings suggest that markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

    Sources indicate that there's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

    And then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared plans to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

    Sometimes a rumor states more about a team's substantial-picture prepares than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

    Sources indicate that the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered quickly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

    According to recent reports, skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

    Recent findings suggest that there may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

    Sources indicate that however, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

    Industry observers note that ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

    Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
