    It has been revealed that victor Wembanyama is hard to put into words. Stephen Curry is the only player I can remember thinking of the same way in the post-Michael Jordan era. Nobody else. With Steph and Wemby, you can't fully describe what you've seen. You try, but in the end you just have to see them to understand. It's totally different than anything you've ever witnessed on a basketball court.

    Sources indicate that so here we go again, trying to write about the indescribable Wembanyama, who put 50 points, 19 boards, five blocks and four steals on the Pelicans on Saturday. It feels like we're qualifying one of his "first in history" stat lines about once a week, and indeed, Wembanyama is the first player since blocks and steals became an official stat in 1973 to record those single-game numbers.

    Just take a look at this guy making the greatest basketball players in the world look like children.

    VICTOR WEMBANYAMA BECOMES THE FIRST PLAYER SINCE 1973-74 TO RECORD 50+ PTS, 15+ REB, 4+ STL AND 5+ BLK IN A GAME!🤯 50 PTS🤯 18 REB🤯 5 BLK🤯 4 STL🤯 5 3PM🤯 32 MINSPURS WIN THEIR 14TH IN 15 GAMES. pic.twitter.com/lPKk3jYNjL.

    Sources indicate that before the halftime buzzer had even sounded, Wembanyama had already tallied 32 points, 13 rebounds, three steals and three blocks. That would be a career game for a lot of NBA players. He had played 18 minutes. You can only laugh at this point.

    What was even funnier, however, was Wembanyama's comment after the game, when he took a clear stab at, well, whoever he considers his "peers" to be by calling them out for, shall we say, unethical statistical pursuits.

    It has been revealed that "It is very special," Wembanyama said of reaching the 50-point mark for the second time this season and third time in his career. "But unlike many of my peers, I'm not good at stat-padding. So I haven't reached it as many times as I should have.".

    Victor Wembanyama after scoring 50 points: “Unlike many of my peers, I'm not very good at statpadding.” pic.twitter.com/OAogFCa2oi.

    According to recent reports, so here's what's interesting about this little dig: Wembanyama was definitely guilty of stat-padding his way to 50 in this game. With just more than eight minutes remaining and the Spurs up by 24, Wembanyama could've stayed on the bench after the timeout. The Spurs have made a concerted effort to limit his minutes whenever possible this year. Even in the golden age of comebacks, this game was over.

    In a recent development, but Wemby stayed in and proceeded to take five straight shots on the next five possessions. He was hunting the 50. No question about it. He even admitted as much.

    "The greats of the game, they don't care [about stat-padding]," Wemby noted, via The Athletic. "I don't think Wilt [Chamberlain] thought about that when he had 98 points. ... That stepback 3, going right, that I took, it doesn't correlate with this. It didn't fit to the definition [of ethical basketball], for example. So I did try [to stat-pad] at the end.".

    Industry observers note that good on Wemby for acknowledging his own hypocrisy, but it raises the question: if you just did the very thing you are railing against, why take the jab in the first place? Every player who has been within range of 50 points has gone for it as long as it's not a competitive game in which quality shots still matter. It's not that massive a deal.

    But Wemby has done this before. In December of 2025, after the Spurs had just defeated the Thunder, he mentioned, "I'm just glad to be part of something that's growing to be so beautiful — pure and ethical basketball.".

    According to recent reports, this was a definite jab at Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's foul-baiting. Wemby, meanwhile, has turned into one of the more theatrical floppers in the league. In almost every way, Wembanyama is different than any other basketball player in the world. But when it comes to this ethical, non-stat-padding basketball soapbox he has climbed upon on numerous occasions, the truth is he's just like everyone else. So enough with the jabs.

    It has been revealed that the NFL on Wednesday will debut the first Thanksgiving Eve game in league history, and it could feature the return of a superstar defender. Green Bay Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons is active for the first time this season and cleared to make his first appearance of the year in the contest against the Los Angeles Rams, but it remains unclear whether he will play. Regardless of when it occurs, the All-Pro will soon enter game action for the first time since he tore his ACL and meniscus last year.

    Recent findings suggest that "I would say I feel like I've done everything I possibly could to put myself in position to potentially play on Wednesday, but for sure this season," Parsons said on Monday. "And I'll be looking forward to returning to the field.".

    The Packers could use a lift as they gear up for a run at the NFC North title. If Parsons suits up this week, he could wreak havoc on an injury-riddled Rams offense and guide Green Bay to one of its biggest wins of the year to begin the regular season's final push.

    Recent findings suggest that the Kansas City Chiefs were seeking a similar boost from their top running back, Kenneth Walker III, who missed the last two games with a groin injury. As a contender for the league lead in rushing yards per game, Walker has been instrumental in the Chiefs' offensive resurgence in 2026, and the unit will need to fire on all cylinders to keep up with the Buffalo Bills in one of the NFL's biggest blockbuster battles of the year.

    Walker returned to practice on Tuesday as a limited participant, but the Chiefs are ruling him out for the holiday showdown.

    Below is the latest on all the other injuries that could impact the NFL's Thanksgiving and Thanksgiving Eve slate.

    Parsons' potential insertion into Wednesday's lineup would be a boon to the Packers, who in their last outing surrendered 30 points to the typically silent Minnesota Vikings offense. It would also inject life into a roster that will again be without another of its stars, Josh Jacobs. Green Bay's top running back continues to nurse the finger injury he sustained in Week 9, which required surgery. With Jacobs ruled out for the second consecutive game, the rushing attack could remain a non-factor. The run game is historically bleak, as its 3.1 yards per game is on pace to be the worst by any NFL team since 2000.

    In a recent development, the Los Angeles Rams' injured reserve remains loaded with impactful pass-catchers. Last week, the team ruled superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua out for the season. This week, it was determined that Davante Adams will not return from a torn hamstring for at least another game and that tight end Terrance Ferguson is out for the year. Ferguson will undergo surgery on the injured ankle that put him on the shelf nearly two months ago. None of those three played in the Rams' 34-6 demolition of the Arizona Cardinals, but the caliber of opponent increases significantly on Wednesday, so the hampered passing attack might not be nearly as impactful this time out.

    The Chicago Bears defensive backfield depth took a hit over the last two weeks. Kyler Gordon has not played since Nov. 8 and is trending toward another absence, which leaves open a hole at the starting slot cornerback spot, and backup safety Elijah Hicks entered concussion protocol on Tuesday and was promptly ruled out for the Thanksgiving clash with the Detroit Lions. Chicago's running back rotation is also in flux after Roschon Johnson was carted off the field last week. He is third in line for carries behind D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai, but with the latter playing through turf toe, his presence has become more crucial of late.

    According to recent reports, an already banged-up defensive line in Detroit is in even worse shape coming out of the win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. In the wake of Aidan Hutchinson's torn ACL, the Lions also lost rookie Skyler Gill-Howard for the season, as coach Dan Campbell confirmed on Tuesday that the defensive tackle will undergo surgery on his knee. And on the edge, DJ Wonnum became all the more important in Hutchinson's absence and is now in danger of missing time himself with the back injury that popped up against the Buccaneers. Campbell noted that all players listed on the injury report outside of Gill-Howard will be game-time decisions.

    It has been revealed that saquon Barkley departed from last week's win with his second stinger of the season and mentioned after the game that he does not expect to be at full strength for the remainder of the season due to multiple lingering challenges. His status for Week 12 was initially up in the air when the Philadelphia Eagles estimated him as a non-participant on Monday, but he practiced in full on Tuesday and should be good to go for the rivalry clash with the Dallas Cowboys. Another positive development was Quinyon Mitchell's return to practice after he missed Week 11 and was listed as a Monday non-participant.

    The Cowboys had no trouble moving the ball without Tyler Booker and Jake Ferguson last week and might have to operate without the starting guard and tight end again on Thursday since neither has been able to practice. The beleaguered Dallas defense, on the other hand, could get two linebackers into action with Jaishawn Barham and Dee Winters both progressing from estimated non-participation to limited participation on Tuesday. The former did not play against the Tennessee Titans, and the latter left that game with a knee contusion.

    In a recent development, if Walker can play in the Thanksgiving finale, the Chiefs will be loaded at running back since Emmett Johnson starred in his absence as a premier rookie ball carrier. Whoever operates in the run game could be without one starting blocker, though, as right tackle Jaylon Moore still has not practiced since he sustained an ankle injury in Week 9. On the other side of the trenches, Omarr Norman-Lott is close to his season debut after the Chiefs activated him from the reserve/PUP list last week.

    Sources indicate that most of the players listed on the Buffalo Bills' injury report sustained their ailments in Week 10 against the Newly introduced York Jets. Christian Benford, Dalton Kincaid, T.J. Sanders and Dorian Williams all missed last week's matchup with the Miami Dolphins as a result of their injuries. It is a positive sign to see all of them practice in at least a limited capacity, but Sanders missed the entire previous week. O'Cyrus Torrence's ankle problem would be a significant one if it keeps him out of action against the Chiefs, because the right guard has not missed a game since he was drafted in 2023.

The No. 2 through the No. 6 seeds in the Eastern Conference standings all have exactly six losses, and while the Philadelphia 76ers hold a three-game lead for the No. 1 seed, they've done so behind a preposterous 12-0 clutch record. When they regress to the mean, we seem destined for an Eastern Conference packed like sardines.

    Industry observers note that the Western Conference is similarly crunched. The San Antonio Spurs and Los Angeles Lakers sit atop the standings with identical 14-3 records... but seeds 3-9 are all separated by no more than two games. Even the Sacramento Kings got a win this week! The NBA has spent years tinkering in order to create parity, and right now, at least it's getting it. With that unofficial week of parity in the books, let's crown some winners and losers from the last seven days.

    Sources indicate that you're expecting me to talk about Wemby's 50-point, 18-rebound, five-block, four-steal performance against the New Orleans Pelicans, aren't you? That'd be the easy starting point. We could just as easily kick things off with Luka Dončić's shooting dip, as he has quietly shot roughly 41-31-82 in his past five games, bringing his ridiculous offensive numbers down to slightly more mortal levels and making Wembanyama, for now, the slight MVP betting favorite. Totally reasonable. They're both contributors to his excellent week.

    Sources indicate that neither stands up to what Wembanyama did against the Los Angeles Clippers on Thursday. He shunked. That's a word that didn't exist when we woke up on Thursday. It is now, hilariously, a signature moment of Wembanyama's young career. He has apparently dunked so often, so violently that he suffered a hand injury that compelled him to try, and succeed, to shoot a jump shot at the rim.

    According to recent reports, did Wemby just... shoot it from above the rim??? 🤯😲 pic.twitter.com/1YDxy8mwy8.

    According to recent reports, the MVP race is for the season. The ridiculous numbers are for the history books. The shunk wins the week. Any time you suffer and overcome a dunking-related injury by inventing a upcoming form of scoring, you win the week.

    Sources indicate that the champs have won five in a row and are 11-3 overall since their 0-3 start, but this isn't as simple as the Knicks suddenly looking like the Knicks again. Many of the early season problems are still persisting. Mikal Bridges hit the game-winner on Friday and still shot 3-of-12 on Sunday. Josh Hart missed all four of his 3-pointers on Sunday and is below 26% shooting from deep so far this season. The starters, as a group, are still getting outscored by almost 13 points per 100 possessions after struggling mightily in the past two regular seasons.

    Yet they just keep winning. There are obvious basketball reasons for that. Karl-Anthony Towns is getting every rebound, making every shot, and has readopted the playmaking hub role he thrived in throughout the postseason, particularly when it comes to assisting Jalen Brunson. The bench is thriving. Landry Shamet is shooting better than 45% on 3s and Deuce McBride isn't far behind. Tyler Kolek has a 61-to-9 assist-to-turnover ratio.

    Recent findings suggest that but there's something deeper here, a resilience and versatility that developed over last season's championship run that is sustaining thus far this season. OG Anunoby has missed the past two games. Towns missed the Blazers game. Bridges and Hart play most of some games and only parts of others because of their early season struggles. Yet Mike Brown just keeps pulling the right levers, and the Knicks just keep figuring it out. Championships can bring about this certainty. The Knicks aren't quite themselves yet, but they have an internalized confidence that came from dominating the playoff crucible a year ago that's paying off handsomely right now.

    It's hard to tell what we've seen from the Heat thus far this season that really deserves scrutiny. They started 0-4 in part because opponents weren't missing any 3s. They've gone 8-2 since, but they haven't beaten a single notable, fully healthy opponent during their active seven-game winning streak. No Evan Mobley against the Cleveland Cavaliers. No Jalen Duren against the Detroit Pistons. No Amen Thompson against the Houston Rockets. No... basically anyone against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Sunday, though in fairness, Giannis Antetokounmpo missed that game himself. Miami is something of a Rorschach test so far. You're going to see what you're predisposed to seeing.

    But if we're going to panic during the shooting luck-induced losing streak, we're going to have to acknowledge the positives during the winning streak. The maligned Heat offense ranks in the top five over their past 10 games largely because Klay Thompson is shooting like Klay Thompson again and Giannis Antetokounmpo never stopped dunking like Giannis Antetokounmpo. Their core lineups featuring Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are deterring rim attempts and giving up basically no corner 3s. Andrew Wiggins looks more like Andrew Wiggins since moving to the bench. As tempted as I was to give the third slot to the player development coaches for the Memphis Grizzlies after Cam Spencer's breakout 26-point game against Cleveland, the seven-game Miami winning streak gets the nod.

    The Celtics were too clever by a half with their lineup decisions this weekend. They sat Jayson Tatum and Derrick White against the hapless Kings and then sat Paul George in the second half of that back-to-back against the Stephen Curry-less Golden State Warriors. They lost both very winnable games by a single point when they probably could have ensured a split and maybe even a sweep by aligning the rest. Throw in a 17-point blown lead to the Denver Nuggets and allowing a 40-point fourth quarter against the Orlando Magic and the previously 11-2 Celtics lost all four of their games this week. They're back with the Eastern Conference pack.

    It's too early to draw any real conclusions, just as it was too early to crown them Eastern Conference favorites when they were throttling the Sixers two weeks ago, but this week was a reminder of some of the cracks here. Their best player is coming off of a torn Achilles, and their second- and third-best players are in their 30s and have to be managed carefully throughout the season. You can get away with never getting to the basket as a team when you're an elite 3-point shooting outfit. The Celtics haven't been this season, and we're now in Year 2 of Derrick White's 3-point drought (and, for that matter, arguably Year 3 of Jayson Tatum's). Mitchell Robinson will put together a few good stretches and then regress back into the mess he's been for most of the season. Boston has been nearly 22 points stronger per 100 possessions with him off the floor this season.

    The Celtics, given their playing style and roster makeup, are vulnerable to the ebbs and flows of an 82-game season. When everyone's available and they're making their shots, they're going to look unbeatable. This week is what happens when they're not, and considering how frequently that's been the case for them in the playoffs, it's something the Celtics are going to have to learn to play through if they hope to make it through this crowded East.

    Industry observers note that slowly but surely, the NBA's cellar dwellers are starting to come around. The Utah Jazz won twice this week. The Chicago Bulls have won three times since Caleb Wilson went down, and they pushed the Denver Nuggets to overtime on Sunday. The Kings got win No. 2 on Saturday, but also pushed the Los Angeles Lakers to the brink on Friday. There is still a whole lot of misery at the bottom of the standings, but all of these teams can find small pockets of optimism.

    Not the Bucks, who are now the NBA's last one-win team and owners of a 13-game losing streak. One of those losses came against Miami this week as their former franchise player, Antetokounmpo, throttled them for three quarters before they made the final score look respectable in the fourth quarter. They have the NBA's worst defense comfortably. Beyond a three-game stretch in which second-year guard Kasparas Jakučionis averaged 21 points per game, it's simply been a miserable season in Milwaukee, and it's one that could get worse any day now as the NBA investigates potential salary cap circumvention involving Gary Trent Jr. We all knew the Bucks would struggle with post-Giannis life, but this is worse than anyone could have imagined.

    It has been revealed that tyrese Haliburton has played four games this season at a roughly All-Star level. The Indiana Pacers are now 3-10 in all other contests, and ESPN reported Friday that Haliburton is set to miss at least another few weeks with a left hamstring strain. This is after a 19-win season played entirely without Haliburton a year ago. At this point, obvious as it sounds, it's simply become clear that the Pacers can't win consistently without their best player. That was obvious in a playoff context, but the regular-season implications here are starting to add up.

    Industry observers note that indiana is already six games out of a top-six Eastern Conference seed. Even when Haliburton gets back, he's probably not going to be perfectly healthy for the entire rest of the season just given his own history of durability concerns. The East's bottom four teams are thankfully so dreadful that there's probably a floor of No. 11 here, but Indiana will eventually have to pass someone -- presumably the Washington Wizards, perhaps someone else who gets bitten by the injury bug -- just to make it back into the Play-In Tournament picture. Even if they're there, their road to and through the playoffs becomes enormously precarious. It doesn't matter how dangerous you are in a playoff setting if you can't actually survive the regular season and make it there. It's too early to say that's where Indiana is headed, but the danger is very real.

    #119106. Industry News: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Red Wings notch massive win in blockbuster NHL deal with Canadiens

    Industry News: Dylan Larkin trade grades: Red Wings notch massive win in blockbuster NHL deal with Canadiens

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams announced on Sunday.
    • In addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal.
    • Larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the Detroit Red Wings have traded former captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster trade, the teams announced on Sunday. This deal ends a bitter saga between Larkin and the Red Wings, and Montreal gave up a king's ransom to make it happen.

    In addition to Larkin, Detroit sent a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick to Montreal. The Red Wings received forward Kirby Dach, goaltender Sam Montembeault, prospect Michael Hage, first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fourth-round pick.

    Larkin requested a trade back in June, and his relationship with the Red Wings only grew more acrimonious with each passing day. As training camp opened in September, Detroit revealed that Larkin had been stripped of his captaincy, and Larkin was booed by fans on opening night at Little Caesars Arena.

    After recovering from an injury he suffered in camp, Larkin played 10 games before announcing that he would be sitting out in anticipation of the trade. While sitting out, Larkin racked up major fines, but his trade request has finally been granted.

    When he's on the ice, there's no denying that Larkin can make a significant impact. The 30-year-old Larkin just notched 34 goals and 33 assists for the Red Wings last season -- his fifth straight year hitting the 30-goal mark -- and he was instrumental in Team USA ending its lengthy gold medal drought at the 2026 Olympics.

    In his career, Larkin has totaled 278 goals and 371 assists in 818 games. The first game Larkin — a native of Waterford, Michigan — plays for the Habs will also be the first he's ever played for a team based outside the Wolverine State.

    It has been revealed that larkin will give the Canadiens much-needed center depth, and he'll be under contract for a while. He's in the fourth year of an eight-year contract that pays him $8.7 million per season.

    This trade fills a void that's existed in the Canadiens' lineup for several years now. Nick Suzuki has evolved into a legitimate star and a franchise-caliber No. 1 center. Beyond him, Montreal has struggled to find a true second-line center.

    Larkin absolutely fits that bill. While he was a bit miscast in Detroit as a first-line center, Larkin is one of the best No. 2 options in the NHL, and he gives the Canadiens an elite one-two punch down the middle.

    Industry observers note that did the Canadiens overpay a bit for a 30-year-old second-line center? In a vacuum, they did. However, taken in context, this deal makes plenty of sense for the Habs.

    Montreal's championship window is just now opening. It already has an elite young core locked up for the next several seasons on team-friendly deals. Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Ivan Demidov, Juraj Slafkovsky, Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson are all 27 or younger and make less than $10 million per season.

    It has been revealed that that gives general manager Kent Hughes a bit more freedom to be aggressive on the trade market. Picks and prospects are nice, but they don't do much good for a team looking to make the jump to contender status in 2026-27. Besides, the Canadiens have been building their prospect pool for years now. It's time to flip some of those assets for proven star power.

    Industry observers note that the Canadiens paid a premium to acquire Larkin. There's no two ways about it. However, Montreal fills a major need and looks a lot more formidable in the Eastern Conference. The Stanley Cup window is officially wide open for the ascending Canadiens. Grade -- B+.

    Consider the situation interim general manager Shawn Horcoff faced. Everyone knew that Larkin wanted out of Detroit so badly that he was paying not to play for the Red Wings.

    On top of that, Larkin had a full no-trade clause, and his list of approved teams amounted to no more than a dozen.

    Should I also mention that Horcoff was thrust into this role in the midst of the offseason, when franchise legend Steve Yzerman was effectively fired for mishandling the Wings' rebuild?

    Given all of that, it's hard to see this as anything less than a home run for Detroit. In fact, it's probably more like a grand slam. Not only did the Red Wings get multiple first-round picks and a couple useful NHL players out of the deal, but they also landed a legitimate blue-chip prospect in Hage.

    Recent findings suggest that the No. 21 pick in the 2024 NHL Draft, Hage is off to a roaring start at the University of Michigan this season with five goals and 21 assists in just 13 games. Detroit might have replaced one franchise center with another one, assuming Hage continues to develop at this rate.

    This was a great piece of work from Horcoff, who probably just made a strong case for the full-time general manager gig in Detroit. This haul will allow the Wings to kickstart another retool or swing a significant trade to bolster the current roster. Either way, the outlook just got a lot brighter in Hockeytown. Grade -- A+.

    NFL on Thanksgiving cheat sheet: Everything you need to know to impress relatives during three holiday games

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Thanksgiving is finally here, and that means the family gets to gather around the table and share one thing we all know and love …football games with stakes!
    • It has been revealed that in this game between two divisional heavyweights, we're going to focus on the trenches when the Lions have the ball.
    • Take this play against the Saints as an example.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Thanksgiving is finally here, and that means the family gets to gather around the table and share one thing we all know and love …football games with stakes! If we include the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and Rams and the Black Friday game between the Steelers and Broncos, all five Thanksgiving Eve/Day/Black Friday games have major implications for both the AFC and NFC playoff races. Some of the league's best are playing on Turkey Day, so just for you, I've put together a special Thanksgiving plate of matchups to watch for on Thanksgiving Day. Let's hop in and establish some fun!

    It has been revealed that in this game between two divisional heavyweights, we're going to focus on the trenches when the Lions have the ball. Since adding DT Jeffrey Simmons, the Bears' defense has taken a major leap in efficiency. According to TruMedia, the Bears have the 4th-best Defensive EPA per play and Defensive Success Rate since Week 8, and a large part of that is Jeffrey Simmons lifting the Bears' defense to new heights. What's really stood out is that with Simmons on the field, Bears' defensive coordinator Dennis Allen can really unlock his Rolodex of coverages on 3rd down without resorting to blitzing as much. Before Simmons came around, the Bears had a 39.3% blitz rate on 3rd down, and when they didn't blitz, their 43.2% pressure rate was 15th in the NFL. Since adding Simmons, their blitz rate on third down has dropped to 25.7%, while their pressure rate without blitzing has risen to 46.2%. With Simmons on the field, Allen can use those blitz looks to scheme up 1v1 chances for Simmons, or force teams to show attention to him that frees up his teammates.

    Take this play against the Saints as an example. It's 3rd and 4, and the Bears line up in a BOSS (Big On Same Side) front, meaning three of their defensive linemen (including Simmons) are lined up on the defense's right, and LB TJ Edwards is lined up over the right guard. In this moment, the Saints are forced to slide the protection to the three defensive linemen and leave the right guard to block Edwards. At the snap, Allen changes the picture, dropping Edwards and giving Simmons a 1v1. Simmons wins instantly and forces Shough out of the pocket and into a pass short of the sticks.

    Sources indicate that this will be Simmons and the Bears' biggest test since the trade, as they face a Lions offense that has been hitting all the right notes. Since their last loss in week four, the Lions are fourth in the NFL in Offensive Success Rate, fifth in EPA per play and fifth in points per drive. Offensive coordinator Drew Petzing has done a really good job of mixing in his own unique flavors to the Detroit offense, but what I really think has helped the most is the offensive line stability and growth. Penei Sewell has fully settled in at left tackle, Christian Mahogany has taken back over at left guard after a suspension and center Juice Scruggs has rebounded from his rough play early in the season to provide stability after starter Cade Mays got hurt. Petzing has gotten creative with his pass protection around Goff (see: the Minnesota game), but the step up in pass pro is due to the overall quality of the OL and some impressive blocks by Jahmyr Gibbs and Sione Vaki.

    In a recent development, against the Bucs, Goff and the Lions absolutely ripped passes down the seams of the defense, and the pass protection did their job to let those chunk plays happen. This one is a five-out play, where all five eligible receivers are out into the passing concept if Vaki doesn't get a blitzer. Look at how pristine this pocket is. Mahogany takes his man and deposits him across the formation as well.

    It has been revealed that this game is going to be all about trench warfare, as the good Lord intended. There's definitely going to be a lot of points, but when you watch this game as you sit down for your first plate of food, keep an eye on the offensive line for the Lions as they try to handle the Jeffrey Simmons problem.

    According to recent reports, this one doesn't quite have the same juice we might've thought it would coming into the season — it doesn't even have the same juice we thought it would a month ago. But it's a rivalry game nonetheless, and for the Cowboys it's a chance to stay alive in their hopes of winning the division. These teams have played before this season, and while some of the faces might look different, the objective for Dallas remains the same:.

    "Run the ball." - Georgia Tech head coach Brent Keypic.twitter.com/yFuipSdv3a.

    Sources indicate that since the win against the Eagles, the Cowboys have run for over 100 yards twice in four games, and since Week 8 Dallas is fifth in EPA per designed rushing attempt (which excludes scrambles) and rushing Success Rate. Part of this emergence has been the offensive line play, which came into the season as a strength and has weathered injuries to get better at the right time. But the other part of it is Brian Schottenheimer getting a little more creative with his run schemes. Through the first seven weeks of the season, Dallas felt like their offense was static. Since Week 8, their motion rate at the snap has ticked up, and it especially has jumped up in the run game. The motion usage and creativity were on display when Kavontae Turpin ran in a 22-yard touchdown against the Titans. Turpin is lined up in the backfield, and the RB goes in orbit motion around him. Then, Dallas runs pin and pull to get their linemen in space against cornerbacks. Advantage: Dallas.

    Tyler Guyton, Tyler Smith and Cooper Beebe all had killer blocks on this Turpin TD run off pin n pull. #Cowboys pic.twitter.com/9HTr0OqWoR.

    Philadelphia is coming off one of their best performances against the run, holding the Steelers to their lowest success rate on designed carries since the first game of the season. What was most impressive about the performance was their tackling, especially by the linebacker group. Pittsburgh's offense relies heavily on yards after the catch and yards after contact, and in their game against the Eagles, they only had one tackle avoided on rushing attempts and 1.80 yards after contact per carry. The Eagles rely heavily on their linebackers to flow fast to the ball in the run game; living in light run boxes requires your linebackers to be real players.

    According to recent reports, outside of Zack Baun, it hasn't always been perfect, but LB Jeremiah Trotter Jr. might've played one of his best career games. He was decisive and fast, filling the run and making a bunch of splash plays in space.

    It has been revealed that heck of a game for Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Sure helps when the #Steelers don't block you on half their runs.Reminds me of another #54. Fred Warner in the '23 opener when he dominated all game. Ground game doesn't stand a chance with LBs running free. pic.twitter.com/U7H2gPQaZZ.

    Second-year LB Jihaad Campbell hasn't been as consistent, but even he had his flashes on Sunday. If you're looking to watch something, anything during this game, look at how the Cowboys run the ball against an Eagles front coming off a really good performance.

    The nightcap might be the most anticipated game of the Thanksgiving Day festivities, as we get another battle between two of the best QBs of the 2020s. Kansas City heads to Buffalo in a game that could also decide home-field advantage in the AFC. The biggest matchup is obviously going to be which defense can slow down the opposing QB, but for this one I'm choosing to focus on the Bills' defense, which is playing sound football, going up against a now-multifaceted Kansas City offense.

    Very slowly, the Chiefs' passing game has rounded into form since their week seven debacle against the Seahawks. Since Week 8, the Chiefs are fifth in the NFL in Success Rate and fourth in the NFL in EPA per play, but if you just take their passing offense since adding WR Josh Downs, the number goes to a 52.6% Passing Success Rate and their EPA per pass has jumped up from 0.17 to 0.22. What Downs has given the Chiefs is another savvy route runner who easily finds holes in zones and creates separation when the Chiefs need him to. Downs is third on the Chiefs in targets since being traded to Kansas City, and you can feel his presence on the field when finding holes in zones.

    This was a fun play for Downs that highlights his ability to find holes in zone coverage and make himself available. The Cardinals are running Cover 6, with the Cover 2 corner to Downs' side. Kansas City is running a Sail concept, with Downs running the "sail" part of the route. Instead of running into the coverage, Downs sits and finds the hole between the two defenders as the go route clears the outside cornerback. Results in an easy first down for the Chiefs.

    3rd and Josh Downs, this time in KC. Downs made a couple of these plays, out routes settling into holes of zones from the slot. He and the emergence of Cyrus Allen have given the Chiefs offense more layers pic.twitter.com/rzk4xinRFH.

    On the flip side, the Bills' defense hasn't allowed a touchdown on 43 straight possessions, one shy of an NFL record set in 2019 by the Latest England Patriots. Yes, the offenses they've played haven't been super impressive, but what they've done to get their secondary turned around is pretty notable. Through the first seven weeks, the Bills were a Cover 3 and Quarters team, asking their DBs to match and communicate as routes were being passed off. Since week 8, they've played much more Cover 2 as their changeup to Cover 3, meaning fewer guys have to run and match and more guys using physicality at the line of scrimmage and driving on routes quickly.

    I think this fits more of the personnel that the Bills have. I've always loved CB Christian Benford in more of a physical, press alignment to get eyes and hands on the receiver, and rookie CB Davison Igbinosun is tailor-made for that style of football. The trade for S Amani Hooker gives them a playmaker on the back end, and everything is tied together much more. Again, this is against the Dolphins, but this is good work by the Bills, rotating into an inverted Cover 2.

    One of the coverage changeups the Bills have leaned into has been Tampa 2 invert/non traditional Tampa like the one here, with Bishop in the flat (cloud) and Igbinosun as a deep half player. This particular one is also paired with a creeper pressure pic.twitter.com/mXe1L6F2HN.

    In a season where there's so much parity, having Bills-Chiefs be a massive game feels right. Both teams are angling for the top seed in a loaded conference, with offenses that are peaking at the right time. It's the perfect ending to an awesome day of football. Happy Thanksgiving, y'all.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As the 2026 Major League Baseball offseason continues to unfold, something vitally important to the future of the sport quietly hums in the background: the ongoing negotiations over a upcoming collective bargaining agreement.

    According to recent reports, the collective bargaining agreement, or CBA (or Basic Agreement, as it's known in a formal sense), is the negotiated accord between players and clubs -- i.e., the team owners and commissioner Rob Manfred, who represents their interests -- that governs the working relationship between the two parties, typically for a period of five years. It covers things as mundane as players' meal allowances and travel protocols and as vital as minimum salaries, the structure of free agency, revenue-sharing specifics, and roster sizes. Every CBA can be distilled down to a fight over money, or, more specifically, how the league's revenues will be divided between players and team owners.

    The first CBA covered the 1968 and 1969 seasons and was the first in professional sports history. That was the handiwork of Marvin Miller, the pioneering head of the Players Association (i.e., the players union) and belated Hall of Famer. It was Miller's organizing skills, foresight, and training as a union economist that allowed him to make the Players Association a viable and effective labor organization. Every CBA negotiation from 1972 through 1994-95 resulted in some form and scale of labor stoppage, whether a players' strike or an owner-implemented lockout. After the cancellation of the 1994 World Series because of the worst labor stoppage in the sport's history, a long run of peace followed. That peace lasted until the prior CBA negotiations, which resulted in a 99-day lockout forced by team owners and delayed the start of the 2022 season.

    According to recent reports, the current CBA negotiations have been underway for some time, and not surprisingly, the two sides remain far apart on several key problems. The biggest fight will be over the owners' renewed desire to implement a salary cap, which the union continues to view as a non-starter. The push for a cap has less to do with the notions of competitive balance and more to do with the ownership's internal belief that being the only non-salary-capped league among the major North American sports is harming franchise values. The cap, though, is but one of many pressing issues on which players and owners must find congruity.

    It has been revealed that moving forward, the process will be uncertain and rife with posturing and pointed public comments from both sides. The hope, though, is that a new CBA will be agreed to before the middle of March 2027, at which point there's a high risk of having the 2027 season delayed or even abbreviated.

    To keep you informed of the twists and turns along the way to a upcoming CBA, we've provided a detailed timeline of negotiations. That timeline will illuminate the important and finer points of the talks and, along the way, explain the implications of the various proposals coming from each side. The hope, of course, is that all of it culminates in a timely agreement that permits a fully intact and on-time 2027 season.

    Recent findings suggest that the owners of Major League Baseball have rolled out legal action against the MLBPA, reports the Wall Street Journal. The lawsuit is a preemptive shot by the league, asking the court to declare that the forthcoming lockout is legal "under antitrust law and cannot be enjoined by a court -- even if the players give up their union status, as the league anticipates they will.".

    The lawsuit names eight defendants, the members of the MLBPA's executive subcommittee: Tarik Skubal, Paul Skenes, Chris Bassitt, Marcus Semien, Jake Cronenworth, Brent Suter, Pete Fairbanks and Cedric Mullins.

    Industry observers note that "MLB believes that the MLBPA is planning to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative and then argue that the lockout constitutes an illegal group boycott. Players would then theoretically have standing to sue the league on antitrust grounds, exposing MLB to the possibility of having to pay treble damages, or three times the players' proven losses.".

    In earlier iterations of negotiations, MLB proposed a salary-escrow system like the ones found in the NBA and NHL. This would mean a percentage of player salaries is withheld in case league revenue projections fall short for a given year. If that's the case, then that money in escrow goes back to the league to cover the revenue shortfalls. If revenues are higher than projected, that excess is shared with the players. The MLBPA has pointedly opposed the escrow system on the grounds that it undermines the notion of guaranteed player salaries. In its latest statement on the negotiations, MLB withdrew the escrow proposal. "For months, union leadership has attacked the escrow provision used in other sports and mischaracterized the glitch as the end of guaranteed contracts," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said in a statement. "MLB took another step today by withdrawing our escrow proposal, removing any doubt that every single guaranteed player contract will remain fully guaranteed in the fresh salary cap and floor system.".

Instead of holding back player money each year, MLB's new proposal is to take that same amount of money out of players' pockets in the following year. It's a different way of achieving the same objective of the salary cap - to reduce and suppress player salaries and freedom of movement. This is yet another example of how MLB's salary cap proposal pits player against player, past, present, and future.".

    In their latest bargaining session, the MLBPA maintained its previous proposals aimed to increase revenue sharing support for small market teams, including a mechanism designed to punish teams that do not put revenue sharing funds into the roster. "Any supposed benefits to certain classes of players are simply taken out of the pockets of other players and are vastly outweighed by the negative effects of the cap and MLB's other restrictions. These negative effects include, but are not limited to, a drastic reduction in overall player compensation and benefits, the end of fully guaranteed contracts, and dramatic restrictions on players' career choices and freedom to contract.".

    Recent findings suggest that "There should be no illusions about the owners' true motivation in pushing for this system. They want to make more money in profits and franchise values by artificially suppressing player salaries.".

In that respect, we've wasted months of time when we could have been having a serious negotiation. So I'd say the more the league is focused on things other than bargaining with us in good faith, I would say that's counterproductive.".

    Meyer also stated the MLBPA has put forth proposals intended to promote competitive balance and correct the game's revenue disparity, but the owners are focused on a salary cap to "increase their profits and franchise values." He added that the two sides have made progress on non-economic matters, such as drug testing and gambling policies.

    To allow for a "smoother transition" to a salary cap/floor system, MLB proposed delaying its implementation until 2028. That would give teams time to prepare and get their payrolls in order, and allow for a full offseason heading into the system. The current competitive balance tax and revenue sharing system would remain in place in 2027.

    Sources indicate that "We recognize that clubs will need a full offseason to prepare to operate within the cap and floor system. Therefore, with this offseason already underway, we proposed today to begin the cap and floor system in 2028," MLB spokesman Glen Caplin remarked in a statement. "This proposal would allow a smoother transition into the cap and floor system.".

    In its latest proposal, MLB proposed reducing the regular season from 162 games to 154 games, and adding a standard off day to every week. The league also proposed extending the Division Series from a best-of-five to a best-of-seven, and allowing higher seeded teams to select their opponents in the Wild Card Series and Division Series. As with every MLB proposal to date, the 154-game schedule and changes to the postseason format are contingent on the MLBPA accepting a salary car/floor system.

    It has been revealed that if labor strife lops off 60 or more games from the 2027 MLB season, then the consequences could be significant. The Athletic recently reported that if the forthcoming lockout extends into late May or so and costs at least 60 games, then most of the league's national broadcast and streaming contracts would be extended for another year, through 2029. That's significant because commissioner Rob Manfred hopes to bundle and centralize team streaming rights and share those revenues equally, and the current timeline would theoretically allow that to happen at the same time the national contracts are up for renegotiation. Tacking on another year to those national contracts would push back the significant windfall that owners and the league are expecting from that latest media rights structure. As such, this is a heavy incentive, at least on the league side, to not let any labor stoppage drag into June.

    More face-to-face negotiations take place, and MLB proposes more changes to the free-agency system, among other asks. MLB's latest proposal includes the following, all of which depend upon the union's acceptance of a payroll cap:.

    Industry observers note that MLB and the owners publicly announce their first formal CBA proposal. Chiefly, they propose:.

    According to recent reports, using competitive balance tax (CBT), or luxury tax, payrolls as a guide, since they include benefits expenses, nine teams at present would be above the proposed cap line, while 12 teams would be below the floor. However, as Craig Goldstein points out, the amount needed to get all these teams below or above the relevant payroll thresholds amounts to an $18.7 million loss in aggregate player salary overall. Another sticking point will be how league revenues are defined. Owners no doubt seek to carve out things like real estate developments surrounding ballparks and ownership stakes in regional sports. As well, MLB's working definition of league revenues includes many expense deductions.

    On another level, the fact that Manfred is able to persuade large-market, high-revenue clubs to agree to equal sharing of all local revenues is a notable development. However, such a concession by those large-market clubs may be contingent upon the implementation of a cap.

    Another sticking point is that the league proposes an escrow system, as is used in the NBA and the NHL. This would mean a percentage of player salaries is withheld. If revenues fall short of projections, some of that money in escrow goes back to the league. If revenues are higher than projected, that excess is shared with the players. The MLBPA opposes the escrow system on the grounds that it undermines the notion of guaranteed player salaries.

"Our goal is to preserve and improve baseball's market system, rewarding competition on and off the field. Additionally, the players' proposals provide increased revenue sharing initially guaranteeing every small market club a minimum of $240m in revenue every season. This enhanced revenue sharing includes added protections to ensure clubs prioritize winning over profiteering. Ultimately, our proposals are designed to build upon the incredible momentum and popularity of our sport world-wide.".

For example, under the Union's proposal, the Dodgers would pay less in luxury tax payments, giving them an additional $70 million to spend on payroll.".

    Negotiations on a new CBA formally begin between teams and players. Among the key issues to be discussed will be the league's desire for a salary cap, drastic changes to the revenue sharing system, league expansion, possible further playoff expansion, and an international draft.

    The 2022-26 Basic Agreement is set to expire at 11:59 p.m. ET, at which point owners are expected to lock out the players in the absence of a new agreement.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open.
    • But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Significant Board.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the first thing to know about the 2027 draft cycle is that it remains wide open. There are still eight months to go before Adam Silver steps up to the podium to announce the first pick. Nothing has been decided yet. In fact, there's probably only about ten players total that can confidently say they expect to be a first-round pick at this point. Everything else is yet to be determined.

    But after three full weeks of college basketball and heading into a Thanksgiving week full of high-profile matchups, we have updated the 2027 NBA Draft Significant Board.

    Industry observers note that inside the front offices of the 30 NBA organizations, most have yet to even start ranking prospects. They're still building their lists, sorting them into tiers, and will spend the coming months trying to establish their order.

    Industry observers note that that's the biggest difference between those front offices and the public discourse about the draft. The fans want answers now, and the Twitter scouts are quick to make bold statements in hopes of saying they were right first. The experts who actually do this for a living recognize that the sole goal is to be right on draft night, and doing that requires them to not jump to any early conclusions.

    That's all critical context to understanding this significant board update, which is, at best, a way too early look at the most relevant prospects. It should be interpreted in tiers. There are probably five or six prospects competing for the top of the draft, but that list could change. Maybe 11 who should feel good about their chances to be first-round picks. Everything beyond that is simply a battle that will continue to play out over the course of the next 8 months. Let's dive into the biggest storylines after three weeks of college basketball action.

    I got a first-hand look at Stokes last week at the Player's Era 8 in Las Vegas. He went down with a contusion midway through his first game, sat out the second, and returned to drop 22 points and 11 rebounds in the final. In totality, the signs of extreme growth that have characterized his early season play continued to be evident in Vegas. He was far and away the most talented player in high school basketball a year ago, but had developed a history of not living up to his potential, or at least not impacting winning to the degree that someone with his talent should. So, coming into his year at Kansas, the eyeballs were more about his maturity, reliability, and approach. Answering those questions has gone about as well as it possibly could so far. He's not only been engaged and impactful, but he's shown connectivity with Bill Self that makes him look coachable. He's also not gotten easily derailed by adversity, which is a reassuring data point.

    To be clear, for as good as he's been, there's still plenty of room for improvement. In high school, he had an instinctive way of improvising his way to the rim. In college, he's found that isn't quite as easy, even with someone like Tre Kaufman-Renn regularly clearing the way for him anytime he comes charging at the rim. So, while he's over-dribbling at times, his playmaking is real, he's asserted himself as a rebounder, his shooting is progressing, and he's starting to use his size in the post.

    According to recent reports, the bottom line is this: most teams are looking for a potential alpha-type creator with the first pick. Stokes is your best bet in the 2027 cycle, by a relatively large margin at this point, but it's still too early to say he's a lock to go number one. I'd put that at about 70% at this point. Getting to the finish line will require him to continue trending in the right direction, making sure teams are comfortable with their due diligence in the pre-draft process, and also leaving open the possibility for someone else to emerge in the coming months.

    It has been revealed that speaking of ascending prospects, no one has moved the needle more in the first three weeks of the season than Illinois' freshman Quentin Coleman. But for those who track draft prospects 365 days a year, the last three weeks are just a short spurt in what has been a rapid rise over the course of the last 15 months.

    In the 2025 EYBL season, Coleman averaged 11.8 points. 5.1 rebounds and 2.4 assists for a Brad Beal Elite team that won the Peach Jam Championship. To put it plainly, he was a role player, albeit a valuable one, on a team that was built around current Arkansas freshman JJ Andrews and utilized Trey Pearson, who is currently a freshman at High Point, as their primary ball-handler and distributor.

    According to recent reports, as soon as Coleman's high school season began, though, we immediately saw signs of growth. Those signs continued throughout the course of the year, and he skyrocketed the rankings in the process. He also decommitted from Wake Forest and took a much bigger NIL payday from Illinois. While he finished with five-star status, it was immediately clear at the USA Basketball trials in May that even that was too low.

    Since arriving at Illinois, Coleman has continued the pattern of exceeding expectations. His skill level, feel for the game, defensive instincts, and nose for the ball are all as impressive as expected. The physical transition has been easier than expected. He's continued to develop more burst, physicality, and, as a result, playmaking.

    At the moment, he's moved all the way up to No. 4 on the CBS's current 2027 NBA Draft Big Board, but we're not going to put a cap on what he could do given the unprecedented growth we've witnessed over the last 15 months.

    According to recent reports, there were a number of prospects who had a chance to be first-round picks in last year's draft, who opted to return to college basketball. While most, if not all, of them are probably making more money in college this year than they would have in the NBA, they are also making strides with their game, and in the process, helping their draft stock in what is widely viewed as a weaker draft than last year's.

    According to recent reports, we've been bullish on Amari Allen's chances of helping himself given his newly introduced on-ball role at Alabama, and so far, he's done just that. The 16 points, 6 assists, and 5 rebounds per game on 52/50/82 shooting showcases both the versatility and shooting gains we were banking on. Most of all, though, it's his decision-making with the ball that has been glaring. His usage has gone way up, and his turnovers have gone way down. He has recorded 30 assists against just three turnovers through the first five games of the season. Add his hyper-competitiveness to the equation, and he's certainly helping himself.

    Arizona big man Motiejus Krivas looked like an NBA-ready defender last year. This year, it's been more of the same. He's massive, even by NBA standards, at 7-foot-2 and 260 pounds, but deceptively versatile and very smart with his angles. We're also seeing definite growth offensively, particularly with his skill set facing the basket. Last week's 18-point, 12-rebound, 4-block performance against UConn was one that captured all of his value, and a game that scouts will undoubtedly revisit.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile, his teammate, Ivan Kharchenkov, has gone from a defensive role player to Arizona's featured scorer, and is putting up nearly 23 points, 8 rebounds, and 5 assists per game. To put it plainly, he's been as good of a two-way player as there is in the country, and now looks like he could be trending towards the draft lottery.

    Sources indicate that florida's Thomas Haugh had a chance to be a mid-first-round pick last June, but the variable that gave many scouts pause was his shooting. This year, he's shooting it with much more confidence and rhythm, making 18 of his 34 attempts through his first five games. Simultaneously, he's continuing to do all the little things that made him so intriguing in the first place with his motor, physicality, rebounding, and defensive versatility.

    In a recent development, speaking of shooting, Braylon Mullins is establishing himself as one of the nation's premier shooters, as expected, despite the fact that he's clearly not 100% healthy. Through his first five games, he's made 19 threes on 50 attempts, but it's been the types of shots that have really stood out. He's running all over the court, flying off screens, and making threes on the move, all while being the focal point of opposing defenses. In short, Mullins is making the type of tough shots that translate to the next level, despite not having his typical ability to separate.

    One of the defining characteristics of the national 2026 recruiting class was the number of prospects who had glaring potential, but had yet to put it all together. That list included the likes of Duke's Cameron Williams,  Ohio State's Anthony Thompson, Maryland's Baba Oladotun, Christian Collins,  Adonis Rayliff and Darius Ratliff, all at USC. Nevertheless, almost all of them commanded the type of recruitment and correlating financial commitment that suggested programs were willing to invest in their development.

    It has been revealed that so far In t those investments have not resulted in the types of gains we had hoped for. The Ratliffs, Adonis in particular, have highlighted some flashes, while Collins has only recently been cleared. Williams and Oladotun are barely in the rotation, and Thompson is playing, but not making the type of impact that anyone hoped.

    Now, despite the lack of immediate return at the college level, most NBA decision-makers are still playing the long game, so I wouldn't expect any of these guys to be given up on just yet. Nevertheless, their early struggles did have to be accounted for on the big board, which is why many of them are now outside the top 30.

    #119102. Industry News: Agent's Take: The Puka Nacua predicament and where his future with Rams stands after injury

    Industry News: Agent's Take: The Puka Nacua predicament and where his future with Rams stands after injury

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2262 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Puka Nacua has nobody to blame but himself for a $5.77 million salary this year while playing out his four-year rookie contract.
    • Nacua started his career like gangbusters.
    • Industry observers note that nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, all career highs, last season.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Puka Nacua has nobody to blame but himself for a $5.77 million salary this year while playing out his four-year rookie contract. Based strictly on production, the 2023 fifth-round pick should have already become the NFL's highest-paid wide receiver ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who received a four-year contract extension averaging $42.15 million per year with a wide receiver record $120.1 million in overall guarantees in March. Instead, Nacua created his own problems.

    Nacua started his career like gangbusters. He set single-season rookie records with 105 receptions and 1,486 receiving yards in 2023. The receptions record has since been broken, but the receiving yards mark still stands.

    Industry observers note that nacua led the NFL with 129 receptions for 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns, all career highs, last season. The 129 receptions are tied as the seventh-best single-season total in league history, and Nacua's 107.2 receiving yards per game led the NFL last year. He also carried the ball 10 times for 105 yards with a touchdown.

    However, the Los Angeles Rams weren't comfortable giving the two-time All-Pro a massive payday during the offseason because of off-the-field problems. Nacua tried to sneak live streamers into the Rams practice facility against head coach Sean McVay's wishes late last season. During the livestream, Nacua performed a suggested touchdown dance with a gesture considered antisemitic, for which he apologized. More concerning, a lawsuit was filed against Nacua in March alleging he bit a woman while intoxicated and made antisemitic statements on New Year's Eve. Nacua spent time during the offseason in a holistic care facility to focus on personal growth and overall behavioral improvement.

    The 2026 season hasn't gone how the Rams and Nacua expected. The Rams were heavy preseason favorites to win Super Bowl LXI before the season started. A 6-4 record after 10 games didn't seem imaginable. But that's the case. Making the playoffs won't be easy, and the Rams have the NFL's hardest remaining schedule.

    According to recent reports, A performance comparable to 2025's, when Nacua was an NFL Offensive Player of the Year finalist, while putting his troubles behind him would have provided ammunition to push for becoming the NFL's highest-paid non-quarterback, as fellow wide receivers Justin Jefferson and Ja'Marr Chase did in 2024 and 2025 on their respective deals with the Minnesota Vikings and Cincinnati Bengals. But that distinction currently belongs to Houston Texans edge rusher Will Anderson Jr., who signed a three-year, $150 million extension averaging $50 million per year (with $134.1 million of guarantees).

    Sources indicate that anderson-type money is no longer a possibility. Nacua's fortunes took a turn for the worse when he suffered a sprained MCL, sprained PCL and turf toe in his right leg at the end of Week 9's win over the Washington Commanders. Nacua wasn't initially put on injured reserve, which requires a four-game absence, because the hope was he would miss about a month of action. A hip/groin problem also kept Nacua out of the Week 2 and Week 3 games.

    The off-the-field transgressions took center stage again last week when the NFL suspended Nacua three games for violating the personal conduct policy. In a controversial but not unprecedented move, Nacua is being allowed to serve his suspension while on IR. Since Nacua was already going to miss these games, the suspension is essentially just a fine of three weeks' salary costing Nacua $961,167.

    It was later revealed that Nacua is out for the season after having surgery to repair his torn MCL last Tuesday. The NFL reportedly was unaware that Nacua had undergone surgery when imposing the suspension two days later.

    According to recent reports, nacua now finishes the 2026 season with 70 catches for 715 yards with four touchdowns in seven games. He was tied for the NFL's third-most receptions and ranked seventh in receiving yards following Week 9. Nacua's 102.1 receiving yards per game are second in the league.

    The expected four- to five-month recovery time means Nacua won't be healthy before free agency begins on March 11. Speculation that Nacua has played his final game for the Rams is premature, but McVay gave mixed messages about Nacua on Monday. He stressed Nacua's importance to the team but couldn't guarantee his return next season.

    In a recent development, it's unlikely the Rams are going to let Nacua walk out the door via the open market. The Rams would only get a 2028 third-round compensatory draft pick at best for Nacua signing with another team in free agency.

    Nacua appears to be destined for a franchise tag in the offseason before the 15-day designation period expires March 3. Under the NFL collective bargaining agreement's formula for non-exclusive franchise tags, the 2027 wide receiver number is projected to be 8.86% of the 2027 salary cap. That's down from this year's 9.063%.

    That means the 2027 wide receiver franchise tag should be $28.661 million, with next year's salary cap being set at $323.5 million. A 7.4% increase in the salary cap over the current $301.2 million figure would be consistent with the 7.88% growth from 2025.

    The non-exclusive tag allows a player to negotiate with other NFL teams. If an offer sheet is signed with another club, the player's team has five days to match the offer. Two first-round picks are the compensation from the signing team if the offer sheet is not matched.

    An exclusive franchise tag, typically reserved for quarterbacks, is impractical due to cost. There's a different calculation in this situation: The average of the top five 2027 wide receiver salaries (salary cap numbers with some minor adjustments) at the end of the restricted free agent signing period (April 23). Initially, the non-exclusive number is used as a placeholder and adjusted upwards if the exclusive calculation dictates once restricted free agency ends.

    Industry observers note that the 2027 exclusive wide receiver franchise tag at the moment projects to $42.247 million. Smith-Njigba's wide receiver market-setting average yearly salary is slightly below the projected tag. This number is subject to change depending on fresh wide receiver deals, contract restructures, pay cuts and/or releases between now and then.

    Recent findings suggest that an offer sheet is prohibited with the exclusive designation. A player under an exclusive franchise tag cannot negotiate with other teams. It is a "closed" negotiation.

    Franchise tag: Accommodating the non-exclusive franchise tag shouldn't be an issue. The Rams have the NFL's fifth-fewest 2027 salary cap commitments at $236.997 million with 37 players under contract and a little less than $3.83 million in existing 2026 cap space that can be carried over, according to NFLPA data. The league average is $298.84 million, with 41 players under contract (rounded to the nearest whole number).

    Sign a long-term deal: Nacua surely doesn't want to play under a franchise tag in 2027 after missing out on an opportunity to cash in this year and having another injury-plagued season. The Rams and Nacua would have until July 15 to sign a long-term deal per CBA rules. Nacua's career earnings from his rookie contract are just under $7.75 million. He also missed five games in 2024 because of a PCL sprain in his right knee, so Nacua has only played 51 games in his four NFL seasons. Playing with reckless abandon seems to make Nacua more susceptible to injury than most other wide receivers.

    According to recent reports, nacua receives an offer sheet from another team: Nacua is the type of talent a team would seriously consider signing to an offer sheet under ordinary circumstances. No wide receiver has ever been more productive than Nacua through his first 51 NFL games. Nacua's 383 receptions are the most ever during that span and 28 more than second place. His 4,906 receiving yards are bettered only by Jefferson's 4,975. Nacua's 96.2 receiving yards per game are the most in NFL history.

    However, Durability concerns and Nacua's baggage could limit offer sheet interest even though high-impact non-quarterbacks are being traded for more than two first-round picks.

    It has been revealed that the Chicago Bears acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick from the Tennessee Titans for a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-round pick at the end of October. The Fresh York Jets dealt All-Pro cornerback Sauce Gardner to the Indianapolis Colts for a 2026 first-round pick (16th overall), a 2027 first-round pick and wide receiver Adonai Mitchell at last year's trade deadline.

    Industry observers note that getting draft capital while avoiding a massive investment in Nacua may make sense for the Rams after a Super Bowl-or-bust season. After all, the 2026 and 2027 first-round picks and more were sacrificed to bring in cornerback Trent McDuffie and edge rusher Myles Garrett, the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year. A bust seems more likely since the Rams wouldn't make the playoffs if the season ended today.

    Sources indicate that the Rams could be facing a transition year in 2027 anyway, as there could be major roster turnover. A conscious decision was made to let a stellar 2023 draft class, which includes offensive guard Steve Avila, offensive tackle Warren McClendon Jr., defensive tackle Kobie Turner, and edge rusher Byron Young, in addition to Nacua, play out their rookie contracts. Plus, future first-ballot Hall of Famer Aaron Donald ended his two-year retirement in August to return for a Super Bowl run on a one-year, $20 million deal (worth a maximum of $30 million through incentives).

    Sources indicate that other key Rams, such as wide receiver Davante Adams, offensive guard Kevin Dotson, tight end Colby Parkinson and center Coleman Shelton, will also be unrestricted free agents. Quarterback Matthew Stafford, the reigning NFL MVP, is showing his age (38) and could retire, although he signed a one-year extension for $55 million in May.

    A sign-and-trade would be more likely than an offer sheet if the Rams and/or Nacua want a fresh start. The last wide receiver to be dealt after receiving a franchise tag is Adams in 2022. The Green Bay Packers got a 2022 first-round pick (22nd overall) and a 2022 second-round pick from the Las Vegas Raiders. Adams became the league's highest-paid wide receiver on an extremely backloaded five-year deal.

    Sources indicate that A franchise player hasn't moved for the unmatched offer sheet compensation in over 25 years. Wide receiver Joey Galloway, who received the exclusive designation, went from the Seahawks to the Dallas Cowboys in 2000 for a 2000 first-round pick (19th overall) and a 2001 first-round pick (seventh overall). Galloway signed a deal making him the NFL's then-second-highest-paid wide receiver in connection with the trade.

    Recent findings suggest that shortly after Adams was dealt, the Miami Dolphins acquired Tyreek Hill from the Kansas City Chiefs for five draft picks: 2022 first (29th overall), second and fourth round picks, as well as 2023 fourth and sixth round picks. Hill replaced Adams as the NFL's highest-paid wide receiver on a severely backloaded four-year contract extension as a part of the trade. Hill had engaged in more egregious conduct than Nacua. He was almost three years removed from any allegations when the Dolphins paid him.

    There's a common denominator in each of these cases. A team was willing to give up significant draft capital and pay top dollar to the wide receivers.

    Industry observers note that whether Nacua remains with the Rams long-term, leaves on an unmatched offer sheet or goes through a sign-and-trade, resetting the wide receiver market isn't out of the question. That's despite missing a season's worth of games over his four NFL seasons and having non-football issues.

    Industry observers note that odell Beckham Jr. also missed 17 games in his first four years, like Nacua. A broken left ankle cost Beckham the final 12 games of the 2017 season. The injuries didn't prevent the New York Giants from putting Beckham at the top of the receiver pay scale with a five-year contract extension.

    Recent findings suggest that nacua switched his representation to Win Sports Group in August, so he shares agents with Smith-Njigba. It wouldn't be surprising for Nacua's camp to seek a deal averaging at least $45 million per year, with as much as $125 million in overall guarantees plus somewhere near $95 million fully guaranteed at signing. Both guarantee marks would be new standards for wide receivers.

    Industry observers note that the team that pays Nacua would be wise to insist on a team-friendly structure. This could mean fewer contract guarantees than in the top wide receiver deals and significant per-game active roster bonuses. The primary benefit of the roster bonuses is that they provide a team with some financial relief with injuries. The per-game amount is only payable if the player is on the active roster for that particular game.

    Recent findings suggest that the largest per-game roster bonus at the moment in a wide receiver contract is Christian Watson's with the Packers. Watson has $2.125 million annually ($125,000 for each game active) from 2027 through 2030.

    Sources indicate that A team making a huge financial commitment with Nacua would be betting that he isn't a buyer beware proposition. The return on investment would be poor if Nacua's problems aren't behind him or injuries continued to mount with his physical style of play.
