    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the San Diego Padres have agreed to terms with veteran left-handed reliever JoJo Romero on a free-agent contract, ESPN reports.
    • In a recent development, romero, who'll be going into his age-30 campaign in 2027, is coming off a solid 2026 campaign for the St.
    • According to recent reports, those numbers don't include Romero's work in the postseason during the Brewers' run to the World Series title.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that the San Diego Padres have agreed to terms with veteran left-handed reliever JoJo Romero on a free-agent contract, ESPN reports. It's a three-year deal worth $21 million, according to The Athletic.

    In a recent development, romero, who'll be going into his age-30 campaign in 2027, is coming off a solid 2026 campaign for the St. Louis Cardinals and, after the trade deadline, the Milwaukee Brewers.

    According to recent reports, those numbers don't include Romero's work in the postseason during the Brewers' run to the World Series title. In 8 playoff innings for Milwaukee, Romero pitched to a 1.13 ERA with 11 strikeouts against only one walk.

    According to recent reports, earlier in the offseason, CBS Sports ranked Romero as the No. 31 free agent in the 2026-27 class. Here's part of that write-up:.

    "An appendectomy split Romero's season in two. He was great during the Brewers' postseason run and has been one of the game's better lefty relievers for four years now. His sinker/sweeper attack is plenty good enough that Romero does not have to be sheltered against righties.".

    For his career, Romero has a 3.51 ERA/119 ERA+ with a K/BB ratio of 3.86 across parts of seven MLB seasons. Over the last three seasons, Romero has a 2.91 ERA, which comes to an ERA+ of 140. He served as closer for the Cardinals for part of the 2025 season, which means he has late-inning experience. Across his 252 career relief appearances, Romero has limited left-handed batters to a slash line of .202/.281/.301.

    Industry observers note that last season, the Padres returned to the playoffs in large measure because of their dominating bullpen. However, their most crucial setup man, lefty Adrian Morejon, is presently a free agent and thus may be bound elsewhere this offseason. Romero is no Morejon, but he does profile as a useful bullpen presence, especially if the gains he enjoyed while on the Brewers' watch prove to be sustainable.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    An awful start for the Chicago Blackhawks only got worse on Monday night when the team announced that captain and superstar forward Connor Bedard would miss four months after undergoing right shoulder surgery.

    It has been revealed that on Nov. 17, Bedard injured his shoulder on a face-off and left the ice in a lot of discomfort. After deliberating whether to rehab the shoulder or get surgery to repair the concern, Bedard opted for the latter half. That will sideline him longer now, but it could provide a more permanent fix.

    Bedard missed the first two weeks of the season while recovering from surgery on his left shoulder in the offseason. The Blackhawks captain suffered that injury during summer training -- and that also occurred on a seemingly innocuous play.

    Recent findings suggest that even after Bedard's initial injury, Chicago hoped that the 2026-27 season would be a step in the right direction amid a lengthy rebuild. Instead, the team is on track to finish with fewer points this year than last year -- despite playing two more games.

    Sources indicate that the Blackhawks are 8-14-2, which is good for 30th place in the NHL. Only the aging Pittsburgh Penguins and actively tanking Vancouver Canucks sit below them. The prospects Chicago has drafted in recent years haven't shown adequate process at the NHL level, and they've got no veteran support around them.

    With Bedard out for an extended period of time, the Blackhawks must re-assess their long-term vision.

    Industry observers note that when healthy, Bedard has shown that he can be a true superstar. The 21-year-old has 82 goals and 139 assists in 234 career games, and he began the 2025-26 season on a torrid pace before, well, suffering a shoulder injury.

    Industry observers note that and therein lies the biggest question about Bedard's future as a true force in the NHL. Is this just bad luck, or will his lack of durability prevent him from reaching the potential that's evident when the puck is on his stick? Chicago can only hope its the former, but this isn't the first time Bedard has missed significant time due to injury.

    Industry observers note that this is now Bedard's fourth NHL season, and he's played 70-plus games just once. That was in the 2024-25 season, when he played all 82 games and tallied 67 points.

    Last season, a right shoulder injury forced him to miss 13 games and snuffed out his tremendous start. Months later, Bedard injured his left shoulder after taking a spill during summer workouts. That prompted one surgery, and his latest right shoulder injury prompted another procedure less than five months later.

    I'm certainly not a doctor, but two shoulder surgeries that close together seems concerning, especially for how much the Blackhawks have invested in Bedard.

    In 2022-23, the franchise completely demolished its roster in hopes of landing the No. 1 overall pick. It worked, and Chicago got to draft Bedard, the consensus top prospect in the class. This past summer, Bedard and the Hawks agreed to a five-year contract extension worth $75 million.

    Industry observers note that if Bedard gets healthy and plays anywhere near his peak, that will be a discount. If injuries continue to limit him, the Blackhawks will have a serious problem on their hands, but that probably goes without saying.

    Even with Bedard in the mix, the Blackhawks' rebuild wasn't going particularly well. Chicago hasn't finished above .500 since the 2019-20 season, which was cut short due to the COVID-19 pandemic and was three years before they selected Bedard in the 2023 NHL Draft.

    The upshot of all that stinking is that the Hawks stocked up on premium draft capital. With that, they've built what should and exciting young core for the franchise. Not including Bedard, Chicago has seven skaters who were selected in the top 50 picks of the last five drafts.

    It has been revealed that kantserov has shown scoring touch at the NHL level, Nazar has been inconsistent and flashed upside and Rinzel has started to show signs of progress on the back end. Other than that, none of those young guns are ready for primetime. That's not say they will never get there. In particular, Frondell and Levshunov have the tools to get there.

    It's just that the results have been really ugly to this point. According to Natural Stat Trick, the Blackhawks rank 30th in expected goals share at 42.5%. The team's minus-32 goal differential ranks 31st in the NHL. To put it more succintly, Chicago is getting what it deserves more often than not.

    In a recent development, with Bedard out for the next four months, it's time to see who can sink and who can swim. Stop playing 37-year-old Ian Cole almost 20 minutes per game and let defensive prospects see the ice more. Tyler Bertuzzi has been incredibly ineffective, and his contract is moveable. Trade him to a contender and open up another spot for a young player in the top six.

    Recent findings suggest that if the team doesn't make any progress over the last 60 games of the season, it may be time for a wholesale changes at the top. General manager Kyle Davidson was tasked with orchestrating a rebuild that's going nowhere rapidly. Jeff Blashill is 37-53-16 behind the Blackhawks' bench, and he's 241-314-88 in his coaching career.

    Sources indicate that if Chicago continues to flail at the bottom of the standings, how much worse could it possibly get? A new set of eyes in the front office and a new voice in the locker room wouldn't be the worst ideas.

    Sources indicate that pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the quarterback he developed into a four-time NFL MVP and Super Bowl XLV MVP with the Green Bay Packers, on Tuesday night just shy of the future Hall of Famer's 43rd birthday. Seven-year NFL veteran Mason Rudolph will start in place of the inactive Rodgers for the Steelers on Friday against the AFC West-leading Denver Broncos (8-2).

    According to Rodgers (during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show), he found out about the benching from tight end Pat Freiermuth, who informed him of Pittsburgh's decision to make him inactive for Friday's game.

    Industry observers note that rodgers is being benched after the Steelers (6-4) lost consecutive games following their 6-2 start to the 2026 season. Pittsburgh was crushed 38-18 at the Cincinnati Bengals on "Sunday Night Football in Week 10 before losing 19-16 against the Philadelphia Eagles, a team that was on a seven-game losing streak, in Week 11. In those two defeats, Rodgers averaged under 5.5 yards per pass attempt in consecutive games for just the second time in the past 10 seasons (Weeks 4-5 of the 2024 season). He has never had such a streak span three games.

    In a recent development, rodgers being benched makes sense when watching the tape. He plays the quarterback position not to get hit anymore. He is just shy of his 43rd birthday on Dec. 2, so it makes sense that the 2026 season will be his last. Rodgers completed 30 of his 44 throws for 227 yards and a touchdown and was also the Steelers' leading rusher (29 yards on 5 carries) in the deflating 19-16 loss against the Eagles as Pittsburgh fell behind 13-0 after their first four drives ended in a turnover on downs and three punts, and Rodgers was never able to guide the Steelers out of that hole.

    It has been revealed that he ranks 19th in the NFL in passer rating (86.6) and 28th in expected points added per dropback (-0.11) among 32 qualified quarterbacks this season. He is completing 60.9% for 2,241 yards passing with 16 passing touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Rodgers' average time to throw of 2.85 seconds stands as the sixth fastest in the entire NFL this season. His 543 career passing touchdowns are the third most in NFL history, and he is the league's all-time leader in touchdown-to-interception ratio (4.21, 543-129). His 6.2 yards per pass attempt (26th in the NFL this season) and 86.6 passer rating 19th in the NFL this season) are both the lowest of his 19 seasons as an NFL starting quarterback. Rodgers' 13.6% off target pass rate ranks as the eighth worst in the league this season, according to TruMedia.

    * Led Packers to win in Super Bowl XLV as Super Bowl XLV MVP (2010 season).

    According to recent reports, rudolph will make his 20th career start in his 39th game played on Black Friday against the Broncos. He has a career 64.2% completion percentage with 4,927 yards passing, 30 touchdowns and 22 interceptions for an 84.3 passer rating. Six of his seven NFL seasons have been with the Steelers since Pittsburgh drafted him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft with the 76 overall pick. Rudolph is 9-9-1 in his career as an NFL starting quarterback with 30 passing touchdowns and 22 interceptions in his starts. His last start came in place of an injured Rodgers in Week 12 of the 2026 season at the Chicago Bears in a 31-28 defeat. Rudolph completed 24 of his 31 throws (77.4%) for 171 passing yards, a passing touchdown and an interception for an 86.9 passer rating.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We're now a month into the 2026-27 NBA season, and while we're still weeks away from the unofficial start of trade season (Dec. 15), we've seen enough basketball for teams to at least begin making plans for the upcoming transaction cycle. Teams are starting to know how good they are, what sort of holes they're dealing with and what the market is going to look like as we draw closer to the February trade deadline.

    Recent findings suggest that firm rumors are still in short supply, but we're at least getting some early buzz on who looks to do what in the months to come. So let's check in on what has made the rounds lately.

    According to recent reports, the 14-3 Los Angeles Lakers are headed for a titanic clash with the San Antonio Spurs on Friday that will presumably put one of those two teams in pole position in the Western Conference. Last Friday, however, head of basketball operations Rob Pelinka did a pregame interview with Spectrum SportsNet in which he made it clear he plans to be aggressive ahead of February's deadline.

    Sources indicate that "We'll be active at the trade deadline to shore up things that we see," Pelinka said. "We think this team has a real chance to make a run, so we want to give the group as much talent as we can. Don't want to get too far over our skis with a hot start, because you don't want to get major-headed, but clearly the way it's gone so far, it's been great and we hope it continues.".

    The Lakers are very limited in terms of tradable draft capital because of their substantial July swing for Walker Kessler. They only have one first-round asset available, and it's only swap rights in 2032. They picked up two useful second-round picks in the Deandre Ayton trade, though, giving them three in total. That's not enough for a blockbuster, but it's helpful liquidity. Further, the Lakers are relatively financially flexible going into the deadline as well. They're barely over the luxury-tax line and have around $8 million in room beneath their first apron hard cap, allowing them to potentially make a somewhat unbalanced trade if the need presents itself.

    So, what would the Lakers be looking for at the deadline? Two obvious needs stand out:.

    As Marc Stein noted, the Los Angeles Clippers have moved to a veteran-only starting lineup, with Darius Garland, Rui Hachimura, Derrick Jones Jr., Max Strus and Brook Lopez opening games lately. Brandon Ingram, returning Monday, is sure to join that group, and Kris Dunn is a central part of their rotation. All of these players but Ingram and Garland are on expiring deals, and Stein noted that the Clippers are "regarded as a certain seller" ahead of the trade deadline.

    And, well, that makes plenty of sense. The Clippers were just stripped of five first-round picks in the Kawhi Leonard scandal. Those expiring contracts belong to players who almost certainly won't be a part of the next great Clipper team, but they could help replenish the team's draft capital moving forward.

    The Clippers are, by far, the most versatile seller on the market right now. In theory, they could burnish just about any contender. Need defense? Jones and Dunn have you covered. Offense? Strus and Hachimura are proven playoff snipers. The center market is in the middle of a supply-demand crisis. Lopez has been sensational this season and could give any contender a solid 20 minutes per night. With Keaton Wagler in the building, it's hard to imagine they'd even shut the door on a good enough Garland offer. Expect the Clippers to live in the rumor mill for the next few months. They have several players who could legitimately impact the championship hunt.

    Recent findings suggest that last week, SNY dropped a stunner of a rumor: that the Utah Jazz, loaded with young guards and off to a terrible start, had had internal conversations about pursuing Mavericks guard Kyrie Irving. The rumor didn't make much sense in the moment, and The Salt Lake Tribune reported Monday that the Jazz "don't appear to have any real interest" in the future Hall of Famer.

    Recent findings suggest that they have, however, talked trade with the team we just discussed: the Clippers. Those conversations began with "various Clippers bigs" and have moved on to wing depth, of which the Clippers have plenty. The Jazz are reportedly casting a wide net in pursuit of help.

    The 3-15 Jazz have been among the NBA's biggest disappointments this season. A lot of that has been the result of injuries, with Jaren Jackson Jr. and Lauri Markkanen out now and Jusuf Nurkić having not yet debuted this season. The Jazz are painfully thin in the front court at this point, and the early partnership between Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson in the backcourt has yielded mixed results.

    Casting a wide net makes sense since the Jazz could theoretically use help basically anywhere. More of a playmaking guard to balance out the score-first instincts that George and Peterson bring would make sense. Wing depth, especially defense-first wing depth, would help address a major weakness. Dunn is a former Jazz player. And of course, adding some size to deal with all of those injuries would probably have the biggest immediate impact. Utah doesn't control its own first-round pick this year. The Jazz benefit from losing in no way, and that has seemingly made them eager to try to fight an uphill battle back into the Western Conference Play-In race.
